message.content:
You are implementing one slice in the DeepSeek Harness repository (a plugin-based agent harness on vendored Cordis). Read /home/user/deepseek-harness/AGENTS.md (CLAUDE.md), packages/AGENTS.md, docs/architecture.md (skim), and the package you change: packages/improvement/program (src/index.ts ~1180 lines, src/types.ts, src/ledger.ts, README.md, tests/). Work only inside your worktree. Do not push. Commit on your worktree branch with clear messages; I will merge.

## The slice: program workflow integrity (three requirements)

Context: `dsh-program` runs a program as departments (one git worktree + one session per goal) and then an integration (merges every department branch onto the base revision in an integration worktree and certifies the merged head). A real run of this workflow yesterday exposed three integrity gaps, all recorded under data/proving-ground/2026-09-08-self-assessment-program-artefacts (read its manifest and `resume-refusal.log` for the exact symptoms):

1. **A department certified an uncommitted tree.** The department's checks passed on its worktree while `git status --porcelain` was not empty, so the integration merge did not carry the file ("missing assessment.md") and the integration failed. Requirement: a department is certified only when its worktree is clean (nothing unstaged, nothing untracked that is not ignored) — otherwise the attempt does not certify and the next directive tells the implementer, in model-facing words, that uncommitted work is not delivered and it must commit (find where `<checks_failed>` directives are built in src/index.ts, around the `checksFailed`/attempt loop, and add the clean-tree condition as part of the same pass so the round cap still applies). The certified department record and the `program/goal` (or equivalent) transition event carry the committed revision (`git rev-parse HEAD`) and its tree digest (`git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}`); the integration verifies before merging each department branch that the branch head equals the recorded revision, and fails the integration with a stated reason when it does not (a department that moved after certification is not what was certified).

2. **The integration ran unconfined and edited a department's file.** Requirement: the integration session is confined the way the environment runner seals a cell: when the composition has a read barrier (`ctx.get('readBarrier')`), register `denyFor(agent.session, <the program's worktrees root directory>)` for the integration session (the integration worktree itself stays granted as the session's own workspace — see `sealWorkspace` in packages/improvement/environment-runner/src/index.ts ~line 1094 and the seal note .agents/notes/**/2026-09-08-*seal* for the precedence rule: a denied ancestor never removes the session's own workspace). Also deny each department worktree explicitly if the worktrees root and the integration worktree share a parent such that the parent denial would be the integration's own parent (work out the layout from `worktreePath`; the aim is: the integration reads and writes its own worktree and nothing of any department worktree). Record the denial on the `program/integration` record (e.g. `denied: string[]`) so the log shows what the integration could not reach; a composition without a barrier records an empty list. `isolation` stays `'none'` unless the seal is provable.

3. **An interrupted integration could not resume.** `driveIntegration` always creates the integration session with the deterministic id `departmentSessionId(programId, INTEGRATION_KEY)`; after a crash or kill while `program/integration` is `running`, `resume()` → `close()` → `integrate()` creates the same id again and persistence refuses with "persisted state already owns this identity". Requirement: when the run's last integration record is `running` and the integration session exists in persistence, resume it (`resumeSession`, as departments do) and continue attempts from what its log records (see how `driveDepartment` computes `from` for a resumed department); re-merging already merged branches must be a no-op (check that `git merge --no-ff` of an already-merged branch is tolerated or skipped by checking `git merge-base --is-ancestor`). The resumed integration must not append a second `program/integration running` record with a new session id; it appends a `program/resume`-style record or reuses the existing one — follow the existing resume conventions in this package.

## Tests and evidence (required)
- Keyless tests in packages/improvement/program/tests (program.spec.ts uses tests/harness.ts; program.e2e.ts boots the real fixture under examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/program): add coverage for (1) an uncommitted department is not certified, the directive names the commit requirement, and after the mock commits it certifies with revision + tree digest; the integration refuses a department branch whose head moved; (2) the integration record carries the denied paths when the barrier is composed (if the program fixture composes no barrier, add a second fixture or overlay that does, keyless, mirroring examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/sealed-cell/cordis.yml for the barrier stack, and assert a `read-barrier/denied` when the integration's mock tries to read a department worktree file); (3) kill-and-resume: an integration interrupted while running resumes on the same session id without the identity refusal.
- Per-file 100% coverage on packages/*/*/src is the CI gate: `pnpm run test:coverage -- packages/improvement/program` (or the closest filter; see docs/testing.md). Run `pnpm exec tsx scripts/run-oxlint.ts <changed paths>` and `pnpm exec tsc -b tsconfig.host.json`. Run `pnpm run doc-sync` at the end (bilingual README: if you change packages/improvement/program/README.md, update README.zh.md and re-record the pairing with `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write packages/improvement/program/README.md`).
- Any keyless snapshot under examples/headless-agent/tests that pins program transcripts must be re-recorded with `DSH_SNAPSHOT=refresh pnpm exec vitest run --config vitest.snapshot.config.ts <the one file>` and only the intended files kept (revert unrelated session.jsonl id churn with git checkout).
- Write one bilingual Agent Note (EN + ZH) under .agents/notes/proposed/architecture/ named 2026-09-08-program-workflow-integrity.md / .zh.md following the format of a recent note there (header `# Agent Note:`, `Status: proposed`, language line, sections `## Problem`, `## Proposal`, `## Alternatives considered`, `## Acceptance criteria`, `## Risks`), and re-record its pairing with `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write <en path>`.
- Update packages/improvement/program/README.md (+zh) for the new behaviour and the new record fields.

## Conventions
- Never commit credentials. No model names or model identifiers of the model you are running on in any committed artifact (product aliases like opus/sonnet/haiku and "Claude Code" are fine).
- Every commit message ends with these two trailer lines exactly:
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HEXjzxR7CyMizem5kFAB4C
- Comments state contracts, not narration; no metaphors. Registrations are effects. Misconfiguration fails loud. Branded ids for cross-boundary ids.
- If a requirement turns out impossible as stated, implement the rest and report exactly what you left out and why.

Report at the end: the commit hashes on your worktree branch, the commands you ran with their results (pass/fail), and any acceptance path you could not cover.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- dsh-archive-agent-notes: Use when adding, auditing, pruning, archiving, restoring, or reviewing Agent Notes in deepseek-harness; checks every new note for superseded active records, classifies implemented notes by future decision value, deletes rejected notes that no longer prevent a tempting fallacy, and applies the frozen archived/{kind} triplet and manifest rules.
- dsh-code-review: Use when reviewing a pull request in the deepseek-harness repo — orients the reviewer to this codebase's standards (AGENTS.md conventions, defensive patterns, ADRs, quality gates) and the review-specific checks that code alone can't show
- dsh-doc-site-sync: Use when publishing, updating, moving, or removing DeepSeek Harness documentation website pages; editing website/docs.ts mappings or navigation; diagnosing a page missing from the VitePress site; fixing projected documentation links; or running the docs:dev, docs:check, and doc-sync workflow after website-content changes.
- dsh-doc-standards: Use when writing, moving, reviewing, or auditing documentation in the deepseek-harness repo — choosing hierarchy and detail, separating tutorials from references, checking tutorial progression, trimming doc slop, responding to a verify-doc-budgets failure, or requests like "improve the docs", "audit the docs", "where should this be documented", or "this doc is too long".
- dsh-find-simplifications: Use when working in the deepseek-harness repo to find non-obvious simplification candidates, write proposed Agent Notes or inline TODO/FIXME/XXX notes, audit or coalesce superseded Agent Notes, or fold worthwhile simplification ideas from another PR; especially for dead, duplicated, speculative, over-built, added-then-removed, or hand-rolled-where-a-dependency-exists surfaces.
- dsh-merging-stacked-prs: Use when landing a stack of dependent GitHub PRs (A ← B ← C, where each bases on the one below) onto master, merging a PR whose base is another open PR's branch, or whenever a request mentions "stacked PRs", "PR stack", "dependent PRs", or merging several related PRs in sequence. Requires every same-repository dependency chain to use GitHub's official stacked-PR feature before landing so GitHub owns stack-wide rules, CI, ordering, retargeting, and merge state.
- dsh-pre-push-checks: Use before pushing, force-pushing, marking ready for review, or claiming checks pass on a deepseek-harness branch, and immediately after gh stack sync publishes rewritten branches, to select the smallest tests and checks that cover the outgoing or just-published diff without reflexively running the full repository suite.
- dsh-prose-standard: Use when writing, reviewing, restoring, trimming, or auditing prose in the deepseek-harness repo, including deciding where documentation or comments are required across Markdown, JSDoc, code and test comments, prompts, descriptions, diagnostics, and CLI or UI strings.
- dsh-trim-cot-leakage: Use when auditing or fixing prose that reads like a leaked reasoning transcript — dead design-session citations such as (decision N), audit item codes, or §N of uncommitted drafts; change narration such as "used to", "no longer", "this cut"; stack or review vantage ("a later PR in this stack", "rejected in review"); reviewer-addressed justifications; control-flow narration; or hedged planning residue in comments, JSDoc, docs, or Agent Notes.
- record-browser-gif: Record browser or Web UI interaction demos as optimized GIFs using the available built-in browser, state-based frame capture, and deterministic encoding, then publish to a dedicated assets branch when the task includes attaching the GIF to a pull request. Use when asked to make, record, or generate a GIF that demonstrates a browser workflow, and for every pull request that changes product-user-visible GUI behavior, which MUST include a GIF recorded from the pull request's real server and model flow.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). # AGENTS.md

DeepSeek Harness is a plugin-based agent harness on vendored Cordis: **everything is a plugin**. Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) before changing `packages/`; follow [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md) for documentation.

## Pre-release stance: foundation over blast radius

**Remove this section at the first tagged release.** With no external consumers, prefer the correct foundation over compatibility shims: rename or repackage freely and update every reference together. Backends reject old on-disk formats. SQLite uses monotonic `SCHEMA_VERSION`; `dsh-session` keeps `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` at `0` without a compatibility promise.

## Repository layout

```
vendor/      Vendored Cordis source — manifest + sync procedure in vendor/README.md
packages/    @deepseek-ai/dsh-<pkg> workspaces at packages/<group>/<pkg>/
  core/        product API spine: session, system-prompt, tools, agent, agent-loop
  api/         Remote BFF assembly and Typert RPC gateway
  typert/      type graph generator, loader, and runtime registry
  llm/         LLM capability: Service Definition/Consumer + DeepSeek providers
  e2b/         E2B POC: sandbox + FS/subprocess adapters
  shell/        bash capability: Service Definition + local/pwsh providers + shell Consumers
  subprocess/  subprocess capability + local process-tree provider
  terminal/         persistent sessions
  fs/          filesystem capability + policy
  lsp/         language-server capability
  skill/       skill provider registry + local impl + catalog/loader tool
  web/         web capability: Service Definition + search/fetch providers + tool Consumer
  compaction/     compaction capability + basic provider
  context/     request-context plugins
  subagent/    subagent capability: Service Definition + providers + delegation Consumers
  bundle/      installable dsh --profile patch-layer bundles
  workflow/    workflow capability + worker-thread provider + tool Consumer
  todo/        todo_write tool
  plan/        plan mode as logged state
  preset/      per-session agent composition from preset cordis.yml files
  guard/       loop-hygiene, tool-timeout, session-budget plugins
  self-modification/  the agent inspects/mounts its own plugins
  hooks/       Claude Code/Codex hook bridges + wire-protocol library
  session/     durable session data: persistence, projection, titles, telemetry
  identity/    anonymous identity
  settings/    user-settings capability + file provider
  credentials/ credential-reference capability + env/.env provider
  acp/         automation-only Agent Client Protocol server
  interaction/ approval/interaction capabilities, permission, commands, ask-user
  boot/        shared app-bin glue
  sdk/         JSON-RPC protocol, server, and TypeScript client
  examples/    demo bundles (agent-spine + CLI/ACP/JSON-RPC bins)
  support/     dev/test infrastructure
  util/        zero-dependency utilities
python/      Python SDK and bundled runtime (see python/README.md)
native/      @deepseek-ai/node-addon-landlock-run source of record (see native/README.md)
examples/    Runnable cordis.yml leaves over packages/examples bundles (see examples/AGENTS.md)
.agents/     Agent workflows and Agent Notes (`notes/`)
docs/        architecture, generated catalogs, postmortems, cookbook (see docs/AGENTS.md)
scripts/     repo gates and generators
website/     VitePress projection of selected bilingual docs/ sources
data/        this repository's own transcripts, runs, knowledge packs (see data/README.md)
```

Package groups: [packages/README.md](packages/README.md).

## Commands

```sh
pnpm install            # pnpm workspaces, node ^22.19 || >=24
pnpm run clean           # remove build outputs and residue of deleted packages
pnpm run test           # vitest unit tests
pnpm run test:coverage  # CI coverage gate: per-file 100% on packages/*/*/src
pnpm run test:e2e       # real-API tests; self-skip without DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
pnpm run test:snapshot  # keyless ACP/headless replay vs expected outputs; filter: -t <name>
pnpm run test:snapshot:record  # re-record expected outputs (needs key)
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run lint
pnpm run duplication    # cross-file TypeScript clone detection
pnpm run build          # tsc emits lib/types, tsdown bundles runtime
pnpm run hygiene        # knip + publint + workspace constraints + NodeNext consumer check
pnpm run check:windows-wine  # ONLY when diagnosing a known Windows failure (needs wine); CI owns it
pnpm run doc-sync       # all documentation gates; leaf list in scripts/run-gates.ts
pnpm run website:build  # VitePress build (doubles as dead-link check)
pnpm dsh --profile headless "task"  # run one task from source (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
pnpm run demo:cordis    # the agent modifies its own runtime (needs key)
pnpm run demo:acp       # ACP automation server (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
```

### Host sandbox failures

When `gh`, `pnpm`, build, test, or generator commands fail because the agent sandbox blocks credentials, network, IPC, file watching, or nested `sandbox-exec`, retry unchanged with the narrowest host escalation before diagnosing authentication or project failure. Require sandbox evidence; never bypass genuine test failures or the product sandbox under test.

### Run relevant checks locally

Run checks before pushes via [dsh-pre-push-checks](.agents/skills/dsh-pre-push-checks/SKILL.md); report only commands run. After `gh stack sync`, validate immediately; merge only after checks pass.

- Match evidence to the surface: focused tests for behavior, snapshots for model or user output, `doc-sync` for docs, build/hygiene and built smokes for published paths, real-API e2e for providers.
- Never default to the full suite or repeat a passing check for commit or push. CI owns exhaustive coverage and the platform matrix; rehearse all locally only by explicit request, for CI diagnosis, or an irreducibly repository-wide change.
- `test:coverage`, not `test`, is the CI coverage gate ([why](docs/testing.md)).

## Secrets / .env

Real-API tests and demos read `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, optional `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, and root `.env`. cordis.yml allows `!!js` (never `!js`) under plugin `config` and entry `disabled`; other metadata stays literal, so conditional composition also uses overlays ([primer](docs/cordis-primer.md#loader-configuration)). Never commit credentials. CI e2e skips without a key; [testing.md](docs/testing.md) owns key policy.

## Conventions

- Every npm package is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>`; vendored packages are rescoped ([mapping](docs/rescope.md)) and `private: true`. `@deepseek-ai/cordis` is a peerDependency (+ dev) of every harness package.
- ESM everywhere (`"type": "module"`). Use package names across packages and `.ts` in local relative imports. Config subprocesses run built `lib/` under plain Node; source regressions use their declared launcher ([testing policy](docs/testing.md#test-subprocess-launch-modes)). The `dsh` CLI source launch runs through tsx's ESM-only hook (`node --import tsx/esm`); modules it reaches must stay ESM (no CJS-only exports) — Node's native TypeScript modes are unavailable across the engines range ([source-launch contract](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-29-dsh-source-launch-tsx-esm.md)). Raw/Web `cordis.yml` bare plugins must appear in their resolver manifest's `dependencies`; `verify-cordis-config` enforces it.
- **Registrations are effects**: every contribution goes through `ctx.effect()` / `ctx.on()`; a registry's `register()` returns the disposer.
- **Runtime invariants assert owned relationships.** Check authoritative event streams or mutable data, not service or method presence, plugin metadata or effects, or fixed pure examples. Without a plausible relationship, an explained empty companion is correct ([package invariant rules](packages/AGENTS.md)).
- **Typed events use declaration merging** and merge-extensible maps. Event JSDoc needs `@mode` and payload `@param`; scoped keys absent from payloads need `@dshScopeScan unsupported`. Public service methods document parameters and non-void returns. A `SessionEventMap` member is required-on-read by default — builds that do not know its type refuse the log unless the event carries the envelope's `ignorable: true`; only structural format changes bump `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` ([mechanism](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)).
- **Switch on discriminant tags.** Closed unions end in `assertNever`; merge-extensible unions fall through a documented default.
- **Waterfall listeners MUST call `next()`** to delegate; returning without it short-circuits the chain ([semantics](docs/cordis-primer.md#cordis-waterfall-semantics)).
- **Model-visible ⟺ logged**: anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the session log; a new model-visible input requires a session event.
- **Plugins, not loop changes**: new behavior goes on documented extension points; changing `agent-loop` requires updating docs/architecture.md.
- **A capability seam comprises Service Definition / Service Provider / Consumer roles.** It is complete, never one role; split only when roles evolve independently ([glossary](docs/glossary.md#capability-seam)).
- **Prefer maintained dependencies over hand-rolling** when they genuinely delete owned code and tests ([policy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-26-dependencies-over-hand-rolling.md)).
- **Explicit > implicit at package boundaries**: defaulting is an explicit `resolve(request): Spec` step in the owning implementation, never a hidden `?? default` inside `run()` (the `dsh-shell` request/spec split is the template).
- **No hardcoded tunables in plugins**: deployment-varying choices are validated `Config` fields changeable from cordis.yml; a `DEFAULT_*` constant or test hook is not configurability. Protocol constants, external specs, and security invariants stay fixed.
- **Misconfiguration fails loud** at load when self-contained, otherwise at the earliest resolvable point; never silently skip a missing referent.
- **Opaque cross-boundary ids are branded** (`Branded<B>` from `dsh-brand`), never bare `string`.
- **Trust TypeScript at typed same-process boundaries.** Do not add runtime validation, fallback behavior, or hostile-input tests solely for values the static interface requires; validate at parser/config, queued, model/tool JSON, durable/file, worker, process, and wire boundaries.
- **Source plane vs artifact plane, never mixed.** Static gates and tests resolve workspace imports through tsconfig `paths` to `src` and pass on a clean tree; gates consuming built `lib/` declare that dependency ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **Keep compiler faces explicit.** Each package uses one aggregate except `api/remotes`; repo-wide programs seed a face config, never the root solution ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **An empty `catch` names what it swallows** and why nothing else can reach it; keep the `try` to one statement.
- Do not comment on facts obvious from code.
- **Prefer symmetry for parallel values**; unexplained asymmetry usually signals a missed extraction.
- **Tests describe behavior, not correctness.** Change obsolete behavior with its tests; explain why in the PR.

## alphaXiv
alphaXiv provides access to a database of over 2.5 million academic research papers from arXiv. (computer science, mathematics, physics, statistics, quantitative biology/finance, electrical engineering, NOT biomedical, clinical, or life science papers from PubMed, Cell, Nature) These tools are useful when the user asks about, references, or discusses academic papers, scientific research, scholarly literature, citations, research topics, or anything related to academic work. If the user mentions a research area, methodology, scientific concept, asks for literature reviews, wants to find related work, or asks questions that could benefit from academic sources, consider using the search tools. When the user references a specific paper or asks about its content, the paper content and PDF query tools can help. Prefer searching for and citing real papers over relying on memory alone for research questions. The library tools manage the user's own folders of bookmarked papers: a paper can live in several folders at once, and 'to read', 'reading', and 'completed' are just the default folders rather than exclusive states. The researcher tools answer questions about people: who works on a subject, an organization's roster, where someone is now, who they publish with, and the user's own follows. Results address papers as [ID=<id>] and researchers as [SLUG=<slug>]; pass those values back to the tools that take a paper id or a researcher slug, and render them as https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/<id> and https://www.alphaxiv.org/@<slug> rather than showing the bracketed handle to the user.

## Anthropic_Economic_Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.

# AGENTS.md — Harness Packages

These package-specific rules supplement the repo-wide [conventions](../AGENTS.md#conventions).

- **Plugin exports:** service packages default-export their service class; function plugins named-export `name` / `inject` / `Config` / `apply` and have no default export. Mixing the forms makes the Loader discard the function plugin's namespace ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Optional services use `ctx.get(name)`.** Reserve `ctx.<name>` for declared injections; the property proxy is topology-sensitive, while strict `ctx.get` reads the global service store ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Product-visible plugins require a non-unit REAL-composition test.** Hand-built `ctx.plugin(...)` suites are insufficient. Boot test-only `cordis.yml` through the Loader and app/process; mock only external services or nondeterministic inputs and assert model-visible, durable, or user-visible output. Keep opt-ins out of shipped defaults. [Policy](../docs/testing.md).
- **Initiator-owned private chains derive, then capture.** Under `ctx.agents.withInitiator()`, recover the Agent at each orchestration entry, derive `agent.session`, and let operation-local helpers close over it. Keep `Agent` and `Session` explicit at lifecycle, session-log, service, authority, worker/process, persistence, and wire interfaces; do not widen a leaf helper from `Session` to `Context` merely to hide a parameter ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-15-agent-initiator-scope.md)).
- **Represent one asynchronous operation with one lifecycle controller or transaction.** Separate readiness, cancellation, disposal, reservation, or sentinel state requires an independent owner or settlement point; otherwise fold it while preserving rollback, callback containment, and quiescence.
- **Design Service Definitions for all current Consumers.** Keep tool-schema, Loader, UI, transport, and provider-specific behavior in the Consumer or provider; do not let one Consumer dictate the service contract ([capability-seam rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-06-13-capability-seams.md)). Inverse smell: a public service method with one internal caller — pass a private capability closure instead (`RunCodeBridgeOptions`).
- **Require a current owner and need.** Tie each abstraction, state machine, option, defensive copy, and compatibility path to a current contract or production consumer, and keep behavior in its owning plugin or service.
- **Require evidence for public choices.** Configurability does not justify an unsupported default, public operation set, format, or imported external concept. Use current-consumer evidence or relevant prior art; otherwise require an explicit value or defer the choice.
- **Write model-facing contracts from the model's perspective.** Prompts, tool schemas, results, and diagnostics contain only task-relevant concepts, not UI, transport, or implementation vocabulary. Pin stable model-visible text verbatim and dynamic behavior through snapshots or end-to-end coverage.
- **Enforce a decision in the operation that makes it.** Schema omission, prompt filtering, facades, wrappers, and listener order are not enforcement when direct or alternate callers can bypass them; test denial through the executor.
- **Publish state only at its commit point.** Emit each notification and update derived state only after the operation succeeds; derive caches, prompts, UI echoes, replay, and query views from one authoritative source.
- **Apply bounds to the complete result.** Enforce byte, token, item, and time limits where the complete emitted or retained value, including wrappers and metadata, is known; test tiny and exact limits, oversized single chunks, and multibyte byte limits.
- **Registry contributions prove disposal** through the HMR-safety test required by [testing policy](../docs/testing.md): dispose the fiber and observe removal.
- **Every package owns `./invariant`.** Register the manifest name; check an event/data relation or give empty installers package-specific `No runtime invariant:` reasons. Generated companions, unexplained empties, and ignored reporters fail [`verify-package-invariants`](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-19-package-invariant-runtime-contracts.md).

[Naming rules](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#name-the-role-that-exists):

- **Package tsconfig:** extends `tsconfig.base.json` (Client: `tsconfig.base.client.json`), uses `rootDir: src`, `outDir: lib/types`, and references each workspace dependency plus `runtime-diagnostics/invariants`; registers in exactly one aggregate. Only `api/remotes` splits for generated contracts; ordinary two-entry Client plugins do not ([layout](../docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- `src/types.ts` contains only types — no runtime code.
- Tests live at package level under `tests/`, not `src/__tests__/`.
- A package's README and JSDoc are part of the change: altered behavior (config keys, defaults, error codes, wire fields) updates them in the same commit. `doc-sync` gates what it can; apply [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for complete, concise prose and verify accuracy against code.
- Package READMEs document model, token, and KV-cache effects using the [canonical Model Experience format](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#4-write-the-package-readme).
- Package READMEs put durable consumer gaps and non-obvious maintainer constraints under `## Known Limitations and Deferred Work`; ordinary cleanup stays in its TODO or Agent Note. Packages with none use a justified [allowlist entry](../scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts) ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-10-readme-known-limitations-gate.md)).

222	/** Whether one executed check passed: a zero exit that neither timed out nor was aborted. */
223	function passed(result: ShellRunResult): boolean {
224	  return result.exitCode === 0 && !result.timedOut && !result.aborted

227	/** Keep the tail of longer text inside the bound, marking what was dropped. */
228	function bounded(text: string, maxChars: number): string {
229	  return text.length <= maxChars ? text : `…${text.slice(text.length - maxChars + 1)}`

232	/** Render one executed command's outcome: the exit fact, then whatever it wrote. */
233	function outcomeOf(result: ShellRunResult): string {
234	  const exit = result.exitCode === null
235	    ? `terminated by ${result.signal ?? 'an unknown signal'}`
236	    : `exit ${String(result.exitCode)}`
237	  const written = [result.stdout.text, result.stderr.text]
238	    .map(stream => stream.trim())
239	    .filter(stream => stream !== '')
240	    .join('\n')
241	  return written === '' ? exit : `${exit}\n${written}`
242	}

245	function retryText(failures: readonly CheckResult[]): string {
246	  const listed = failures.map(failure => `- ${failure.checkId}: ${failure.evidence}`).join('\n')
247	  return `<checks_failed>\n${String(failures.length)} of this goal's checks did not pass on the branch as it stands.\n${listed}\nKeep working and commit; the checks run again when you stop.\n</checks_failed>`

568	  private async reconcile(

570	    state: DepartmentState,
571	    sessions: ReadonlyMap<SessionId, ScannedSession>,
572	  ): Promise<boolean> {
573	    const before = state.status
574	    const sessionId = this.departmentSessionId(run.programId, state.goal.key)
575	    const scanned = sessions.get(sessionId)
576	    if (scanned === undefined) {
577	      state.status = 'pending'

580	    state.sessionId = sessionId
581	    const workspace = this.worktreePath(run.programId, state.goal.key)
582	    state.workspace = workspace
583	    if (!await isDirectory(workspace)) {

589	    if (department.certified) {

594	    if (department.phase === 'blocked') {
595	      state.status = 'blocked'
596	      state.reason = department.blockedCode
597	      return before !== state.status
598	    }
599	    state.status = 'running'
600	    return before !== state.status

624	  /** Run departments until none can start, then integrate or close the program. */
625	  private async drive(run: ProgramRun): Promise<ProgramReport> {
626	    const running = new Map<string, Promise<void>>()
627	    let ceilingReached = false
628	    while (!this.stopping) {
629	      const runnable = [...run.states.values()].filter(state => !state.driving && this.canRun(run, state))
630	      for (const state of runnable) {
631	        if (running.size >= this.config.maxConcurrentGoals) break
632	        if (await this.overCeiling(run)) {
633	          ceilingReached = true
634	          break

636	        state.driving = true
637	        running.set(state.goal.key, this.department(run, state).finally(() => {
638	          state.driving = false
639	          running.delete(state.goal.key)
640	        }))
641	      }
642	      if (running.size === 0) break
643	      await Promise.race(running.values())
644	    }
645	    await Promise.all(running.values())
646	    if (this.stopping) return this.report(run)
647	    return await this.close(run, ceilingReached)
648	  }

661	  private async overCeiling(run: ProgramRun): Promise<boolean> {
662	    const ceiling = run.spec.tokenCeiling
663	    if (ceiling === undefined) return false
664	    const { members } = await this.scan()

668	  /** Integrate a fully certified program, or close one that cannot reach that. */
669	  private async close(run: ProgramRun, ceilingReached: boolean): Promise<ProgramReport> {
670	    const states = [...run.states.values()]
671	    if (states.every(state => state.status === 'certified')) {
672	      // A process that died between the integration's certificate and the
673	      // records that follow it finishes the bookkeeping instead of merging
674	      // the same branches a second time.
675	      if (run.integration?.status === 'certified') await this.markMerged(run)
676	      else await this.integrate(run)
677	    }
678	    if (states.every(state => state.status === 'merged')) return await this.release(run)
679	    for (const state of states) {
680	      if (state.status === 'pending') await this.transition(run, state, 'abandoned', 'the program ended before this goal started')
681	    }
682	    run.outcome = ceilingReached ? 'abandoned' : 'failed'
683	    run.session.append('program/end', { programId: run.programId, outcome: run.outcome })
684	    await this.ctx.sessions.flush(run.session)
685	    return this.report(run)
686	  }

688	  /** Record the release of a program whose integration certified its merged head. */
689	  private async release(run: ProgramRun): Promise<ProgramReport> {
690	    this.requireSignoffRecord(run.spec, run.session.events, 'release', 'release')
691	    const mergedRevision = run.integration?.mergedRevision
692	    run.outcome = 'released'
693	    run.session.append('program/end', {
694	      programId: run.programId,
695	      outcome: 'released',
696	      ...mergedRevision === undefined ? {} : { mergedRevision },
697	    })
698	    await this.ctx.sessions.flush(run.session)
699	    return this.report(run)
700	  }

702	  /** Merge every department branch onto the base revision and certify the result. */
703	  private async integrate(run: ProgramRun): Promise<void> {
704	    const workspace = this.worktreePath(run.programId, INTEGRATION_KEY)
705	    const branch = this.branchName(run.programId, INTEGRATION_KEY)
706	    try {
707	      await this.ensureWorktree(workspace, branch, run.spec.baseRevision)
708	    } catch (error: unknown) {
709	      await this.failIntegration(run, String(error))
710	      return
711	    }
712	    run.integration = { programId: run.programId, status: 'running' }
713	    run.session.append('program/integration', run.integration)
714	    await this.ctx.sessions.flush(run.session)
715	    try {
716	      for (const key of dependencyOrder(run.spec.goals)) {
717	        const departmentBranch = this.branchName(run.programId, key)
718	        await this.git(['merge', '--no-ff', '-m', departmentBranch, departmentBranch], workspace)
719	      }
720	    } catch (error: unknown) {
721	      await this.failIntegration(run, String(error))
722	      return
723	    }
724	    const certified = await this.driveIntegration(run, workspace)
725	    if (certified) await this.markMerged(run)
726	  }

733	  /** Record an integration that could not produce a merged head to certify. */

735	    run.integration = { programId: run.programId, status: 'failed', reason }
736	    run.session.append('program/integration', run.integration)

740	  /** Certify the merged head, letting a model fix it when the checks do not pass as merged. */
741	  private async driveIntegration(run: ProgramRun, workspace: string): Promise<boolean> {
742	    const sessionId = this.departmentSessionId(run.programId, INTEGRATION_KEY)
743	    const handle = await this.createSession(sessionId, workspace, undefined, run.programId, INTEGRATION_KEY)
744	    try {
745	      const { agent } = handle
746	      const goal = this.ctx.goals.create(agent, {
747	        objective: `Make the merged head of "${run.spec.objective}" pass its integration standard.`,
748	        maxGoalRounds: this.config.maxGoalRounds,
749	      })
750	      this.ctx.goals.disarm(agent)
751	      this.ctx.completionStandards.author(agent, { goalId: goal.id, checks: integrationChecks(run.spec.integration) })
752	      await this.ctx.sessions.flush(agent.session)
753	      // The merge itself is the first candidate: a clean merge whose checks
754	      // pass needs no model turn at all. The integration is always driven
755	      // through the model route, whatever staffs the program's departments:
756	      // making a merged head pass is this harness's own repair work.
757	      const certified = await this.attempts({
758	        agent,
759	        workspace,
760	        isolation: 'none',
761	        objective: undefined,
762	        from: 1,
763	        work: (prompt): Promise<boolean> => this.turn(agent, prompt),
764	      })
765	      if (!certified) {
766	        await this.failIntegration(run, 'the merged head did not pass the integration standard')
767	        return false
768	      }
769	      const mergedRevision = await this.head(workspace)
770	      run.integration = { programId: run.programId, status: 'certified', mergedRevision, sessionId }
771	      run.session.append('program/integration', run.integration)
772	      await this.ctx.sessions.flush(run.session)
773	      return true
774	    } finally {
775	      await handle.dispose()
776	    }
777	  }

779	  /** Create or resume one department, drive it, and record what it came to. */
780	  private async department(run: ProgramRun, state: DepartmentState): Promise<void> {
781	    const { goal } = state
782	    const workspace = this.worktreePath(run.programId, goal.key)
783	    const sessionId = this.departmentSessionId(run.programId, goal.key)
784	    const resuming = state.status === 'running'
785	    let delegation: ResolvedImplementer | undefined
786	    let handle: AgentHandle
787	    try {
788	      // The staffing is refused before the worktree exists, so a program whose
789	      // implementer this deployment cannot supply costs no branch and no session.
790	      delegation = this.resolveImplementer(run.spec.implementer, goal)
791	      handle = resuming
792	        ? await this.resumeSession(sessionId, goal.preset)
793	        : await this.openDepartment(run, state, workspace, sessionId)
794	    } catch (error: unknown) {
795	      await this.transition(run, state, 'failed', String(error))
796	      return
797	    }
798	    try {
799	      await this.driveDepartment(run, state, handle.agent, workspace, resuming, delegation)
800	    } catch (error: unknown) {
801	      await this.transition(run, state, 'failed', String(error))
802	    } finally {
803	      await handle.dispose()
804	    }
805	  }

807	  /**
808	   * The staffing one department's attempts run under.
809	   * @param implementer - the frozen spec's staffing.
810	   * @param goal - the goal being staffed, whose isolation the provider must support.
811	   * @returns the resolved provider and label, or `undefined` for a department
812	   *   this service drives through the model route itself.
813	   * @throws {@link ProgramError} when the seam or the named provider is absent,
814	   *   or when an out-of-process provider cannot support the goal's isolation.
815	   */
816	  private resolveImplementer(implementer: ProgramImplementer, goal: ProgramGoalSpec): ResolvedImplementer | undefined {
817	    switch (implementer.kind) {
818	      case 'route':
819	        return undefined
820	      case 'subagent': {
821	        const subagents = this.ctx.get('subagents')
822	        const provider = subagents?.getProvider(implementer.provider)
823	        if (subagents === undefined || provider === undefined) {
824	          throw new ProgramError(
825	            `this program delegates its departments to the subagent provider "${implementer.provider}", which this deployment does not compose`,
826	            'PROGRAM_IMPLEMENTER_UNAVAILABLE',
827	          )
828	        }
829	        if (goal.isolation !== 'none' && runsOutOfProcess(provider.capabilities)) {
830	          throw new ProgramError(
831	            `goal "${goal.key}" claims "${goal.isolation}" isolation, which no department delegated to the out-of-process provider "${implementer.provider}" can support`,
832	            'PROGRAM_IMPLEMENTER_ISOLATION',
833	          )
834	        }
835	        return {
836	          subagents,
837	          provider: implementer.provider,
838	          ...implementer.label === undefined ? {} : { label: implementer.label },
839	        }
840	      }
841	      /* v8 ignore next 2 -- ProgramImplementer is a closed union validated at
842	       * the spec boundary; this arm is only the static exhaustiveness guard. */
843	      default:
844	        return assertNever(implementer)
845	    }
846	  }

848	  /** Mint one department's worktree and session, then record it as running. */
849	  private async openDepartment(
850	    run: ProgramRun,
851	    state: DepartmentState,
852	    workspace: string,
853	    sessionId: SessionId,
854	  ): Promise<AgentHandle> {
855	    const { goal } = state
856	    await this.ensureWorktree(workspace, this.branchName(run.programId, goal.key), run.spec.baseRevision)
857	    const handle = await this.createSession(sessionId, workspace, goal.preset, run.programId, goal.key)
858	    const { agent } = handle
859	    try {
860	      agent.session.append('budget/caps', goal.budget)
861	      const created = this.ctx.goals.create(agent, { objective: goal.objective, maxGoalRounds: this.config.maxGoalRounds })
862	      this.ctx.goals.disarm(agent)
863	      this.ctx.completionStandards.author(agent, { goalId: created.id, checks: goal.checks })
864	      await this.ctx.sessions.flush(agent.session)

866	      await handle.dispose()
867	      throw error
868	    }
869	    state.sessionId = sessionId
870	    state.workspace = workspace
871	    await this.transition(run, state, 'running', undefined)

875	  /** Drive one department's attempts until it certifies, blocks, or runs out of rounds. */
876	  private async driveDepartment(
877	    run: ProgramRun,
878	    state: DepartmentState,
879	    agent: Agent,
880	    workspace: string,
881	    resuming: boolean,
882	    delegation: ResolvedImplementer | undefined,
883	  ): Promise<void> {
884	    // A department whose goal is blocked is never driven: the reconciliation
885	    // routes it to `blocked` and waits for an operator's own resume.
886	    const current = this.ctx.goals.get(agent)
887	    if (current === undefined) {
888	      await this.transition(run, state, 'failed', 'the department session carries no goal')
889	      return
890	    }
891	    if (resuming) {
892	      // A department loaded from persistence starts disarmed; the resume edge
893	      // is the durable record that this process took it back over, and the
894	      // disarm that follows keeps the attempts this service's rather than the
895	      // goal-round driver's. A goal the previous process completed without a
896	      // certificate cannot be resumed, and fails the department loudly.
897	      this.ctx.goals.resume(agent, { id: current.id, revision: current.revision })
898	      this.ctx.goals.disarm(agent)
899	    }
900	    const certified = await this.attempts({
901	      agent,
902	      workspace,
903	      isolation: state.goal.isolation,
904	      objective: state.goal.objective,
905	      // A delegated attempt that already ended is recorded, and this pass
906	      // continues after it rather than running it a second time.
907	      from: foldDepartmentLog(agent.session.events).delegated + 1,
908	      work: delegation === undefined
909	        ? (prompt): Promise<boolean> => this.turn(agent, prompt)
910	        : (prompt, attempt): Promise<boolean> => this.delegate(agent, delegation, state.goal.key, prompt, attempt),
911	    })
912	    const settled = this.ctx.goals.get(agent)
913	    if (settled?.phase === 'blocked') {
914	      await this.transition(run, state, 'blocked', settled.blockedReason?.code)
915	      return
916	    }
917	    if (!certified) {
918	      await this.transition(run, state, 'failed', `no certificate after ${String(this.config.maxGoalRounds)} rounds`)
919	      return
920	    }
921	    state.revision = await this.head(workspace)
922	    await this.transition(run, state, 'certified', undefined)
923	  }

925	  /** Deliver one attempt as a user turn to the department this service drives itself. */

927	    agent.followup(createUserMessage({ content: [{ type: 'text', text: prompt }], source: { kind: 'user' } }))
928	    await agent.whenIdle()
929	    return this.ctx.goals.get(agent)?.phase !== 'blocked'

932	  /**
933	   * Run one attempt of a delegated department as one child of the external
934	   * coding agent and record what it came to. The provider derives the child's
935	   * working directory from the department session's own `cwd`, which is the
936	   * department worktree, so the child works on the department branch.
937	   * @param agent - the department session, which is the child's delegating parent.
938	   * @param delegation - the resolved provider and label, already checked against the goal's isolation.
939	   * @param goalKey - the goal this department delivers, recorded with the run.
940	   * @param prompt - the goal text on the first attempt, the check-failure text after.
941	   * @param attempt - the 1-based attempt this run serves.
942	   * @returns `true`, because a run that ended without completing still leaves a
943	   *   tree the department's checks measure.
944	   */
945	  private async delegate(
946	    agent: Agent,
947	    delegation: ResolvedImplementer,
948	    goalKey: string,
949	    prompt: string,
950	    attempt: number,
951	  ): Promise<boolean> {
952	    const child = await delegation.subagents.start(delegation.provider, {
953	      prompt: [{ type: 'text', text: prompt }],
954	      parent: agent,
955	      signal: this.teardown.signal,
956	      ...delegation.label === undefined ? {} : { label: delegation.label },
957	    })
958	    try {
959	      const result = await child.result
960	      agent.session.append('program/delegation', {
961	        goalKey,
962	        attempt,
963	        provider: delegation.provider,
964	        runId: child.id,
965	        stopReason: result.stopReason,
966	        ...result.structured === undefined ? {} : { structured: result.structured },
967	        ...this.delegationUsage(child.localAgent),
968	      })
969	      await this.ctx.sessions.flush(agent.session)
970	    } finally {
971	      await child.dispose()
972	    }
973	    return true
974	  }

976	  /** What one delegated attempt cost, for a child whose own session this process holds. */
977	  private delegationUsage(child: Agent | undefined): { usage?: ProgramDelegationUsage } {
978	    if (child === undefined) return {}
979	    return { usage: { totalTokens: foldBudgetSpend(child.session.events, {}).totalTokens } }

982	  /**
983	   * Run the session's standard against its workspace, letting the attempt's own
984	   * work happen between runs, until it certifies or the round cap is spent.
985	   * @param plan - the session, worktree, isolation claim, first prompt, first
986	   *   attempt, and the work one attempt does.
987	   * @returns whether a run certified the standard.
988	   */
989	  private async attempts(plan: AttemptPlan): Promise<boolean> {
990	    const { agent, workspace } = plan
991	    let prompt = plan.objective
992	    for (let round = plan.from; round <= this.config.maxGoalRounds; round += 1) {
993	      if (prompt !== undefined && !await plan.work(prompt, round)) return false
994	      const standard = this.ctx.completionStandards.get(agent)
995	      if (standard === undefined) return false
996	      const ref = { id: standard.id, revision: standard.revision }
997	      const results = await this.execute(standard.checks, workspace)
998	      const outcome = this.ctx.completionStandards.recordRun(agent, ref, plan.isolation, results, { executor: 'runner' })
999	      await this.ctx.sessions.flush(agent.session)
1000	      if (outcome.certified) {
1001	        const goal = this.ctx.goals.get(agent)
1002	        if (goal !== undefined) this.ctx.goals.complete(agent, { id: goal.id, revision: goal.revision })
1003	        await this.ctx.sessions.flush(agent.session)
1004	        return true
1005	      }
1006	      this.ctx.completionStandards.issueDirective(agent, ref, {
1007	        rootCause: `${String(outcome.failures.length)} of this goal's checks did not pass`,
1008	        detail: bounded(outcome.failures.map(failure => `${failure.checkId}: ${failure.evidence}`).join('\n'), this.config.evidenceMaxChars),
1009	      })
1010	      prompt = retryText(outcome.failures)
1011	    }
1012	    return false
1013	  }

1015	  /** Run every active check in order through the shell executor rooted at the worktree. */
1016	  private async execute(checks: readonly StandardCheck[], workspace: string): Promise<CheckResult[]> {
1017	    const results: CheckResult[] = []
1018	    for (const check of checks) {
1019	      const result = await this.ctx.shell.run(this.ctx.shell.resolve({ command: check.run, workdir: workspace }))
1020	      results.push({
1021	        checkId: check.id,
1022	        status: passed(result) ? 'pass' : 'fail',
1023	        evidence: bounded(outcomeOf(result), this.config.evidenceMaxChars),
1024	      })
1025	    }
1026	    return results
1027	  }

74	/**
75	 * Fold one persisted session into its program ledger.
76	 * @param session - the stored header and log.
77	 * @returns the ledger, or `undefined` when the log carries no `program/start`
78	 *   and is therefore not a program session.
79	 */
80	export function foldProgramLedger(session: ScannedSession): ProgramLedger | undefined {
81	  let start: ProgramStart | undefined
82	  let integration: ProgramIntegrationRecord | undefined
83	  let end: ProgramEnd | undefined
84	  const goals = new Map<string, ProgramGoalRecord>()
85	  for (const event of session.events) {
86	    if (event.type === 'program/start') start = event.data
87	    else if (event.type === 'program/goal') goals.set(event.data.key, event.data)
88	    else if (event.type === 'program/integration') integration = event.data
89	    else if (event.type === 'program/end') end = event.data
90	  }
91	  if (start === undefined) return undefined
92	  return {
93	    sessionId: session.meta.id,
94	    start,
95	    goals,
96	    ...integration === undefined ? {} : { integration },
97	    ...end === undefined ? {} : { end },
98	  }
99	}

101	/**
102	 * Fold one department session's log into what it states about its own work.
103	 * @param events - the department session's stored log, oldest first.
104	 * @returns the certificate presence, the goal phase, the blocking code, and
105	 *   the last delegated attempt the log records.
106	 */
107	export function foldDepartmentLog(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): DepartmentLog {
108	  const certified = events.some(event => event.type === 'verification/certificate')
109	  const goal = foldGoal(events).goal
110	  let delegated = 0
111	  for (const event of events) {
112	    if (event.type === 'program/delegation') delegated = Math.max(delegated, event.data.attempt)
113	  }
114	  return {
115	    certified,
116	    delegated,
117	    ...goal === undefined ? {} : { phase: goal.phase },
118	    ...goal?.blockedReason === undefined ? {} : { blockedCode: goal.blockedReason.code },
119	  }
120	}

128	 * @returns the membership, or `undefined` when the session carries no stamp.

131	  for (const event of session.events) {
132	    if (event.type !== 'program/member') continue
133	    return {
134	      programId: event.data.programId,
135	      key: event.data.key,
136	      sessionId: session.meta.id,
137	      totalTokens,
138	    }
139	  }
140	  return undefined
141	}

143	/**
144	 * Tokens every session of one program already spent.

146	 * @param programId - the program whose sessions to sum.
147	 * @returns the summed input plus output tokens; `0` for a program with no session yet.

152	    .reduce((sum, member) => sum + member.totalTokens, 0)

168	    abandoned: 0,

126	  // missing field would reject every program a deployment does not gate on one.
127	  signoff: z.object({
128	    artefactSha256: z.string().required(),
129	  }).default(undefined as unknown as ProgramSignoff),
130	  tokenCeiling: z.natural().min(1),
131	}) as z<ProgramSpec>
132	
133	/** Reject a budget field that cannot express a ceiling. */
134	function requireBudget(key: string, field: string, value: number | undefined): void {
135	  if (value === undefined) return
136	  if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0) {
137	    throw new ProgramError(`goal "${key}" budget ${field} must be a finite non-negative number, got ${String(value)}`, 'PROGRAM_INVALID_SPEC')
138	  }
139	}
140	
141	/** Reject a check inventory that cannot author a standard. */
142	function requireChecks(owner: string, checks: readonly StandardCheck[]): void {
143	  const seen = new Set<string>()
144	  for (const check of checks) {
145	    if (seen.has(check.id)) {
146	      throw new ProgramError(`${owner} declares check "${check.id}" twice`, 'PROGRAM_INVALID_SPEC')
147	    }
148	    seen.add(check.id)
149	  }
150	}
151	
152	/** Reject a dependency list that names an unknown key, itself, or one key twice. */
153	function requireDependencies(goal: ProgramGoalSpec, keys: ReadonlySet<string>): void {
154	  const seen = new Set<string>()
155	  for (const dependency of goal.dependsOn) {
156	    if (dependency === goal.key) {
157	      throw new ProgramError(`goal "${goal.key}" depends on itself`, 'PROGRAM_INVALID_SPEC')
158	    }
159	    if (!keys.has(dependency)) {
160	      throw new ProgramError(`goal "${goal.key}" depends on "${dependency}", which the program does not declare`, 'PROGRAM_INVALID_SPEC')
161	    }
162	    if (seen.has(dependency)) {
163	      throw new ProgramError(`goal "${goal.key}" depends on "${dependency}" twice`, 'PROGRAM_INVALID_SPEC')
164	    }
165	    seen.add(dependency)
166	  }
167	}
168	
169	/**
170	 * Order the goals so every goal follows the goals it depends on.
171	 *
172	 * Ties break by key, so one dependency graph always merges in one order and two
173	 * processes integrating the same program produce the same merge sequence.
174	 * @param goals - the program's goals; their dependencies must be resolvable.
175	 * @returns the goal keys in dependency order.
176	 * @throws {@link ProgramError} when the dependencies contain a cycle.
177	 */
178	export function dependencyOrder(goals: readonly ProgramGoalSpec[]): string[] {
179	  const pending = new Map(goals.map(goal => [goal.key, new Set(goal.dependsOn)]))
180	  const ordered: string[] = []
181	  while (pending.size > 0) {
182	    const ready = [...pending.entries()]
183	      .filter(([, dependencies]) => dependencies.size === 0)
184	      .map(([key]) => key)
185	      .sort((left, right) => (left < right ? -1 : 1))
186	    const next = ready[0]
187	    if (next === undefined) {
188	      const cycle = [...pending.keys()].sort((left, right) => (left < right ? -1 : 1))
189	      throw new ProgramError(`goals ${cycle.map(key => `"${key}"`).join(', ')} form a dependency cycle`, 'PROGRAM_INVALID_SPEC')
190	    }
191	    pending.delete(next)
192	    for (const dependencies of pending.values()) dependencies.delete(next)
193	    ordered.push(next)
194	  }
195	  return ordered
196	}
197	
198	/**
199	 * Validate one caller-supplied spec and freeze it.
200	 *
201	 * The staffing default is materialized here rather than read through a
202	 * fallback at each use: a frozen spec states one implementer, the digest covers
203	 * it, and the ledger stores it.
204	 * @param input - the spec as the caller supplied it.
205	 * @returns the validated spec, with every default materialized.
206	 * @throws {@link ProgramError} when a key, dependency, budget, or check
207	 *   inventory cannot support a program.
208	 */
209	export function resolveProgramSpec(input: ProgramSpec): FrozenProgramSpec {
210	  const validated = ProgramSpecSchema(input)
211	  const spec: FrozenProgramSpec = { ...validated, implementer: validated.implementer ?? { kind: 'route' } }
212	  if (spec.goals.length === 0) {
213	    throw new ProgramError('a program declares at least one goal', 'PROGRAM_INVALID_SPEC')
214	  }
215	  const keys = new Set<string>()
216	  for (const goal of spec.goals) {
217	    if (!PROGRAM_GOAL_KEY.test(goal.key)) {
218	      throw new ProgramError(`goal key "${goal.key}" must be lower-kebab-case`, 'PROGRAM_INVALID_SPEC')
219	    }
220	    if (keys.has(goal.key)) {
221	      throw new ProgramError(`goal key "${goal.key}" is declared twice`, 'PROGRAM_INVALID_SPEC')
222	    }
223	    keys.add(goal.key)
224	  }
225	  for (const goal of spec.goals) {
226	    requireDependencies(goal, keys)
227	    requireBudget(goal.key, 'maxTotalTokens', goal.budget.maxTotalTokens)
228	    requireBudget(goal.key, 'maxWallMs', goal.budget.maxWallMs)
229	    requireBudget(goal.key, 'maxCostEur', goal.budget.maxCostEur)
230	    if (goal.checks.length === 0) {
231	      throw new ProgramError(`goal "${goal.key}" declares no check, so nothing can certify it`, 'PROGRAM_INVALID_SPEC')
232	    }
233	    requireChecks(`goal "${goal.key}"`, goal.checks)
234	  }
235	  dependencyOrder(spec.goals)
236	  if (spec.integration.checks.length + spec.integration.gates.length === 0) {
237	    throw new ProgramError('the integration declares no check and no gate, so nothing can certify the merged head', 'PROGRAM_INVALID_SPEC')
238	  }
239	  for (const check of spec.integration.checks) {
240	    if (RESERVED_GATE_CHECK.test(check.id)) {
241	      throw new ProgramError(`integration check "${check.id}" uses an id the program reserves for integration.gates`, 'PROGRAM_INVALID_SPEC')
242	    }
243	  }
244	  requireChecks('the integration', spec.integration.checks)
245	  return spec
246	}
247	
248	/**
249	 * The integration standard: the declared checks followed by one check per gate.
250	 *
251	 * Folding the gates in is what makes the integration certificate cover them:
252	 * the verification domain records one result per active check, so a gate that
253	 * lives outside the standard would be a pass the certificate never states.
254	 * @param integration - the spec's integration section.
255	 * @returns the checks to author the integration standard from, in order.
256	 */
257	export function integrationChecks(integration: ProgramSpec['integration']): StandardCheck[] {
258	  return [
259	    ...integration.checks,
260	    ...integration.gates.map((gate, index) => ({
261	      id: `gate-${String(index + 1)}` as CheckId,
262	      outcome: `the merged head passes the gate: ${gate}`,
263	      run: gate,
264	    })),
265	  ]
266	}
267	
268	/** One check as the digest reads it, free of any property order the caller used. */
269	function canonicalCheck(check: StandardCheck): unknown {
270	  return { id: check.id, outcome: check.outcome, run: check.run }
271	}
272	
273	/** One implementer as the digest reads it, with both arms stating every field. */
274	function canonicalImplementer(implementer: ProgramImplementer): unknown {
275	  return implementer.kind === 'route'
276	    ? { kind: 'route', provider: null, label: null }
277	    : { kind: 'subagent', provider: implementer.provider, label: implementer.label ?? null }
278	}
279	
280	/**
281	 * Digest one frozen spec.
282	 *
283	 * Goals are sorted by key and each goal's dependencies are sorted, so the order
284	 * a caller listed them in never changes the identity; check and gate order is
285	 * kept, because it is the order a validator runs them in. `implementer` is
286	 * covered, because a deliverable staffed by the harness and the same one
287	 * staffed by an external coding agent are two programs to compare rather than
288	 * one program run twice. `signoff` is excluded: it names the artefact the
289	 * program's signatures attest instead of stating what the program runs.
290	 * @param spec - the validated spec.
291	 * @returns the lowercase SHA-256 hex of its canonical form.
292	 */
293	export function programSpecDigest(spec: FrozenProgramSpec): string {
294	  const goals = [...spec.goals]
295	    .sort((left, right) => (left.key < right.key ? -1 : 1))
296	    .map(goal => ({
297	      key: goal.key,
298	      objective: goal.objective,
299	      preset: goal.preset,
300	      isolation: goal.isolation,
301	      budget: {
302	        maxTotalTokens: goal.budget.maxTotalTokens ?? null,
303	        maxWallMs: goal.budget.maxWallMs ?? null,
304	        maxCostEur: goal.budget.maxCostEur ?? null,
305	      },
306	      dependsOn: [...goal.dependsOn].sort((left, right) => (left < right ? -1 : 1)),
307	      checks: goal.checks.map(canonicalCheck),
308	    }))
309	  const canonical = {
310	    objective: spec.objective,
311	    baseRevision: spec.baseRevision,
312	    tokenCeiling: spec.tokenCeiling ?? null,
313	    implementer: canonicalImplementer(spec.implementer),
314	    goals,
315	    integration: {
316	      checks: spec.integration.checks.map(canonicalCheck),
317	      gates: [...spec.integration.gates],
318	    },
319	  }
320	  return createHash('sha256').update(JSON.stringify(canonical)).digest('hex')
321	}
322	
323	/**
324	 * The identity one digest names.
325	 * @param digest - the spec digest.
326	 * @returns `program-<digest>`, which is also the program session's id.
327	 */
328	export function programIdFor(digest: string): ProgramId {
329	  return ProgramId(`${PROGRAM_ID_PREFIX}${digest}`)
330	}
