1	# @deepseek-ai/dsh-program
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	Programs: the durable ledger of one client deliverable decomposed into many goals. A program is a frozen spec, one program session holding `program/*` events, one department session and git worktree per goal, and one integration session whose certificate over the merged head is what a release claims. Every ledger event is appended after the fact it records is durable, so a restarted process reconciles each goal from its department's own log and worktree, never runs a department twice, and never releases without a certificate. A department is staffed either by the harness agent this service drives or, through the subagent seam, by an external coding agent whose attempts it records and whose tree it certifies. The [program-ledger](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-program-ledger.md) and [external-implementer](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-program-external-implementer.md) Agent Notes own the design rationale.
6	
7	## Config
8	
9	```yaml
10	- id: program
11	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-program'
12	  config:
13	    workspaceRoot: /var/lib/dsh/delivery
14	    requireSignoff: true
15	    maxConcurrentGoals: 3
16	    maxGoalRounds: 8
17	    branchPrefix: program
18	    evidenceMaxChars: 2000
19	```
20	
21	| Field | Meaning |
22	|---|---|
23	| `workspaceRoot` (required) | The git repository the program delivers into. Every worktree is minted under it at `<workspaceRoot>/<programId>/<key>`, so the deployment points it at a checkout whose `baseRevision` the program's branches start from. It must be an absolute path the composed shell can carry unquoted, which the plugin checks at load. |
24	| `requireSignoff` (required) | Whether the program session must carry a `signoff/recorded` before departments start and before the program releases. A client district sets it; both refusals carry `PROGRAM_SIGNOFF_REQUIRED`. |
25	| `maxConcurrentGoals` (required) | Departments of one program that run at the same time. Dependencies bound this further: a goal starts only once every goal it depends on has certified. |
26	| `maxGoalRounds` (required) | The round cap every department and integration goal is created with, and the number of validation attempts this service drives before recording a department `failed`. |
27	| `branchPrefix` (required) | Branch namespace of every worktree: `<branchPrefix>/<programId>/<key>`. Lower-kebab-case git ref components. |
28	| `evidenceMaxChars` (required) | Bound of each recorded check evidence and each directive detail. Keep it at or below the verification domain's `maxTextChars`, which refuses longer text. |
29	
30	The service requires `agents`, `agentDefaultModel`, `agentPresets`, `completionStandards`, `goals`, `sessions`, `sessionPersistence`, and `shell`; it reserves the read-barrier run directory when `readBarrier` is composed, and reads `subagents` when a program delegates its departments. `verify-village-composition` counts a composition of this package as a district composition, so it must also carry a capped budget policy, a session persistence backend, and the checkpoint policy.
31	
32	## Service contract
33	
34	`ctx.programs.start(spec)` validates and freezes the spec, resolves its presets, and drives the program the spec identifies: a program whose session does not exist yet is opened, one whose session exists is reconciled instead of forked, and one whose ledger already carries a closing record is reported unchanged. `ctx.programs.resume()` reconciles every program in the persistence root whose ledger has no closing record and carries it on; the plugin runs it once over the settled Loader tree, and an operator or driver may call it again. Both entry points run through one queue, so no program is ever driven by two passes at once.
35	
36	`programSpecDigest(spec)` is the SHA-256 hex over the canonical spec: the objective, the base revision, the token ceiling, the resolved `implementer`, the goals sorted by key with each goal's dependencies sorted, and the integration's checks and gates in authored order. `signoff` is excluded — it names the artefact the program's signatures attest rather than what the program runs, so the same goals signed over two artefacts are one program. `program-<digest>` is the program id, the program session's id, and the prefix of every department session id (`<programId>-<key>`), which is what makes "one session per key" a property of the identity rather than of a lookup.
37	
38	### The two signatures
39	
40	Under `requireSignoff: true`, opening a program reads `signoff/recorded { transition: 'spec-freeze' }` from the program session and releasing reads `signoff/recorded { transition: 'release' }` before `program/end { outcome: released }`; each must attest the digest `spec.signoff.artefactSha256` names, and this service never writes one. The caller records them through `ctx.signoffs` ([`@deepseek-ai/dsh-signoff`](../../governance/signoff/README.md)) on the session `programIdFor(programSpecDigest(resolveProgramSpec(spec)))` addresses — derivable before the program exists, because the program id is the spec digest. `start` continues that log rather than replacing it, so the signatures stay in the same session as the ledger. A program whose release signature is missing refuses at the closing edge and stays open: the next pass reconciles it from its departments and releases once the signature is recorded.
41	
42	`resolveProgramSpec(spec)` refuses a spec before anything runs: a key that is not lower-kebab-case or declared twice, a dependency on itself, on an unknown key, or stated twice, a dependency cycle, a budget field that is not a finite non-negative number, a goal with no check, a repeated check id, an integration that declares neither a check nor a gate, and an integration check claiming a `gate-<n>` id the gates own.
43	
44	## The ledger
45	
46	The service creates one session per program and appends to it, flushing at every step so a process that dies leaves a truthful record.
47	
48	| Event | Written when | Payload |
49	|---|---|---|
50	| `program/start` | Before any department exists | `programId`, `specSha256`, the frozen `spec`, `baseRevision`, `implementer`, and `signoff` — the attested artefact digest — when the spec named one |
51	| `program/goal` | Once per status change, after the fact it records is durable | `programId`, `key`, `status`, and the `sessionId`, `workspace`, `revision`, or `reason` that status carries |
52	| `program/integration` | When the merged worktree exists, then when it certifies or fails | `programId`, `status` (`running`, `certified`, `failed`), `mergedRevision`, `sessionId`, `reason` |
53	| `program/resume` | When a later process picks the program up | `programId` and the reconciled count per status over every goal of the spec |
54	| `program/end` | Once the program is over | `programId`, `outcome` (`released`, `failed`, `abandoned`), and `mergedRevision` for a released one |
55	| `program/member` | At creation, in the department or integration session rather than the ledger | `programId` and the `key` that session works |
56	| `program/delegation` | After one delegated attempt's child run settled, in the department session | `goalKey`, `attempt`, `provider`, `runId`, `stopReason`, and the `structured` result or `usage` the run left |
57	
58	A goal's status is `pending` before it has a department, `running` while one works, `blocked` while it waits for an operator's resume through the goal domain, `certified` once its own log carries a certificate, `merged` once a certified integration covers its branch, `failed` when it ended without a certificate, and `abandoned` when the program ended before it started. The [persistence catalog](../../../docs/persistence-catalog.md) carries each payload's declaration.
59	
60	## Departments
61	
62	A goal starts as a department once every goal it depends on has certified. The service adds a git worktree on `<branchPrefix>/<programId>/<key>` from the base revision, creates the department session through `ctx.agents.create` with `meta.cwd` at that worktree and the goal's preset mounted, reserves the read-barrier run directory when a barrier is composed, stamps the session with `program/member`, appends `budget/caps` with the goal's budget, creates the goal with the configured round cap, and authors the goal's standard from its `checks` — then records the department `running`.
63	
64	The service is the department's validator. It delivers the goal's objective as one user turn, runs the standard's checks through the shell executor rooted at the worktree, and records the run; a passing run certifies, completes the goal, and records `certified` with the branch head that certificate cites. A failing run issues a directive and delivers one more turn, up to `maxGoalRounds` attempts; a department that never certifies is recorded `failed`, and one whose goal reached the blocked phase — a breached budget, for instance — is recorded `blocked` with the blocking code and left for an operator. The service never writes into a department's worktree: whatever the branch head carries is what the department committed.
65	
66	## The two implementers
67	
68	`spec.implementer` decides who writes the code. `{ kind: 'route' }`, the default `resolveProgramSpec` materializes, is the harness agent above: this service drives it turn by turn through the LLM seam. `{ kind: 'subagent', provider, label? }` delegates instead: the department is opened exactly the same way — worktree, session, preset, `program/member`, `budget/caps`, goal, standard — and then each attempt is one `ctx.subagents.start(provider, …)` whose prompt is the goal objective on the first attempt and the same check-failure text a driven department would receive on later ones. Because the department session's `cwd` is the worktree, every shipped provider derives the child's working directory from it without the program passing a path. The run's result is awaited, `program/delegation` is appended and flushed, the run is disposed, and the department's checks then run on the tree the child left. The round cap bounds delegated attempts as it bounds turns, and the integration is always driven through the model route: making a merged head pass is this harness's own repair work.
69	
70	A delegated department is refused before its worktree exists when `ctx.subagents` is not composed or has no provider under that name (`PROGRAM_IMPLEMENTER_UNAVAILABLE`, naming the provider), and when the goal claims an isolation above `none` while the provider runs its child outside this process (`PROGRAM_IMPLEMENTER_ISOLATION`). The second rule is what the level means: isolation above `none` is a claim over what the session's own read-barrier census proves about its executors, and no executor of this process mediated a child in another one. An in-process provider joins the parent's standing composition, keeps that census and role, and may therefore keep the deployment's isolation. Both refusals record the goal `failed` with the reason.
71	
72	**What a delegated certificate proves:** the program ran the goal's checks, through the shell executor, in the department worktree, on the tree the external agent left, and recorded the run and the certificate in the department's own session. That is the whole claim. It proves nothing about how the tree was produced: for an out-of-process provider no model-visible history of the implementer lives in this log, the department's trajectory carries no steps, and `usage` is recorded only for a child this process published and whose own session log accounts for tokens. Because `implementer` is inside the digest, the same goals staffed two ways are two programs — which is what makes comparing them a comparison of certificates over trees rather than of transcripts.
73	
74	## Integration and release
75	
76	Once every goal is certified, the service adds the integration worktree at `<workspaceRoot>/<programId>/@integration` — a key no lower-kebab-case goal key can claim — from the base revision, records `program/integration { running }`, and merges each department branch in dependency order with `git merge --no-ff`. It then creates the integration session over that worktree with a standard authored from `integration.checks` followed by one `gate-<n>` check per entry of `integration.gates`, so the integration certificate covers the gates as well as the checks. The checks run before any model turn, so a clean merge that passes needs none; a merged head that does not pass is what the integration goal is for. The certificate records `program/integration { certified, mergedRevision }`, every goal moves to `merged`, and `program/end { released, mergedRevision }` follows. A merge that fails and a merged head that never passes both record `program/integration { failed, reason }` and end the program `failed`.
77	
78	## Resume
79	
80	`resume()` lists persisted sessions, loads every program session with a `program/start` and no `program/end`, and reconciles each goal from its department's own log and worktree rather than from the ledger: a department session that does not exist is `pending`, one whose worktree is gone is `failed` because the branch is the evidence its certificate cites, one whose log carries a certificate is `certified` with the branch head read from the worktree, one whose goal is blocked is `blocked`, and anything else is `running`. Every status the reconciliation discovered is recorded, together with a declaration for any goal the ledger never recorded at all, before `program/resume` states the counts. Departments that are still running are resumed in place through `ctx.agents.resume` and the goal domain's own resume; pending goals whose dependencies have certified are started. Because a department's session id is derived from the program id and the key, no key ever gets a second session.
81	
82	A delegated department's `program/delegation` records are part of that log, and the highest attempt they carry is what the resumed pass continues after, so an attempt that already ended is never run a second time. The invariant companion holds the same relation for every department session: a `program/delegation` follows the session's `program/member` for the same key and carries an attempt strictly greater than every attempt already recorded there.
83	
84	A program's optional `spec.tokenCeiling` is folded from the usage of every session carrying its `program/member` stamp, at each department start. A program that has spent its ceiling starts no further department, records the goals that never started `abandoned`, and ends `abandoned`.
85	
86	## Git operations
87	
88	Every git command runs through the composed shell under whatever policy that executor applies, in `workspaceRoot` for worktree creation and in the worktree itself for merges and revision reads. The program creates worktrees and branches under its own prefix, merges department branches into its own integration worktree, and reads `HEAD`. It never commits, never writes a file into any worktree, and never touches a branch outside `<branchPrefix>/<programId>/`. Paths and revisions are checked against a no-quoting-needed character set before they reach a command line, because shell quoting is dialect-specific and this service does not know the composed shell's dialect.
89	
90	## Model Experience
91	
92	None, as the ledger records what departments delivered and writes no model-visible input of its own; the goal objective, the standard, and the composed preset own every model-facing effect of a department session, and no `program/*` event ever enters a model request. A delegated department's prompt is the same goal or check-failure text, delivered to the child through the subagent seam rather than to the department's own model; where that text is logged is the child's business, and `program/delegation` records only what the run came to.
93	
94	#### KV Cache effect
95	
96	Independent per department: each department and the integration is its own session with its own request history, and this package neither extends nor rewrites any of them. The one turn it delivers is an ordinary user message appended at the end, so a department's own prefix stays reusable across its attempts. A delegated department sends no request at all, so it has no prefix; each child run's own cache is that provider's concern.
97	
98	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
99	
100	- **The scorekeeper does not fold programs** — the `program/member` stamp is written for it, but no facts group reads it yet, so a program's spend and certification rates are read by hand from the ledger and the member sessions.
101	- **A signature is recorded, not authenticated** — `requireSignoff` gates on a `signoff/recorded` whose principal the deployment's identity provider supplied; nothing here or in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-signoff` verifies that the id names the person who signed.
102	- **The release signature is read at the closing edge only** — a program whose spec freeze is signed but whose release is not runs every department and its integration before refusing, so the refused pass costs the whole program's work; nothing asks for the release signature earlier.
103	- **One program at a time per process** — every pass runs through one queue, so two programs started concurrently are driven one after the other. Concurrency inside a program is what `maxConcurrentGoals` bounds.
104	- **A blocked department needs an operator** — the ledger records the blocking code and stops; nothing re-arms a blocked goal, so a program with one ends `failed` until a person resumes that goal through the goal domain and starts the program again.
105	- **Departments claim their isolation without staging their checks** — the run directory is reserved so the barrier records the session as an implementer, but check scripts are not staged there, so a goal declaring `isolation` above `none` is refused by the verification domain unless the session's own census proves the claim.
106	- **A resumed department keeps its admitted rounds** — the round cap is a property of the goal, so a program that restarts often exhausts its departments' caps sooner; the ledger makes that visible as `failed`.
107	- **A delegated child's spend is outside the ceiling** — `spec.tokenCeiling` folds sessions carrying `program/member`, and a delegated child is either a separate unstamped session or another process entirely. `usage` on the delegation record states what a locally published child cost; nothing bounds an external agent's own billing.
108	- **A delegated attempt is one prompt and one result** — nothing steers a child mid-attempt, so a round cap of `n` buys `n` chances rather than `n` messages, and a program delegating to an external agent wants a smaller cap and a larger per-attempt scope.
109	- **The out-of-process test reads advertised capabilities** — the isolation refusal asks the seam's `runsOutOfProcess`, which treats a provider that advertises no parent-enforced start-time capability as running its child elsewhere, which every shipped out-of-process backend does for exactly that reason; the bridge's `harnessTools` and a product backend's `model` do not count, since the model still runs elsewhere in both. A future backend that runs a child in another process while advertising a parent-enforced one would defeat the test, and the rule would have to move to an explicit marker on the seam.
110	- **The program is the same implementer for every goal** — `implementer` is program-level, so one program cannot staff one goal by hand and another by delegation; comparing two staffings is comparing two program ids.
111	- **A department names no model, so none is forwarded and none is recorded** — the frozen spec's `implementer` carries only `kind`, `provider`, and `label`, so a delegated department runs whichever model the provider defaults to and `program/delegation` records neither the model the child ran nor the spend it reported. The seam already carries all three ([`model` on the start request, `reportedModel`/`reportedUsage`/`reportedCostUsd` on the result](../../subagent/subagent/README.md#capabilities)) and the [environment runner](../environment-runner/README.md#the-two-implementers) forwards and records them; giving the spec a model means extending the frozen spec and its digest, which changes every existing program id.

1	# Agent Note: The sealed cell workspace, a run directory a cell cannot read
2	
3	Status: proposed
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-08-sealed-cell-workspace.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	A fleet lays its cells out as siblings. [`dsh-fleet`](../../../../packages/improvement/fleet/README.md) creates one `cell-<id>` directory per cell directly under the run directory, and the run directory also holds `plan.json`, the run log, and the fixture material every cell of the slot was cut from. Every cell agent runs with its workspace as its cwd and, in the bench composition that produced this repository's records, an unconfined `dsh-bash-local` executor and no read barrier. Its cwd was a convention, not a fence: `cd ..` reached the whole experiment.
10	
11	The cells took the invitation. [`data/proving-ground/tools/census-escapes.mjs`](../../../../data/proving-ground/tools/census-escapes.mjs) reads a recorded run and reports, per cell, the tool calls whose path arguments name the run directory or another cell of the same run. Over the eighteen recorded runs it finds cells that left their own workspace in ten of them: 4 of 12 cells in `2026-09-07-bench-h1-harness-loop-t2`, 11 of 18 in `2026-09-07-bench-h1-harness-loop-t4`, 3 of 36 in `2026-09-07-bench-e2-harness-vs-product-t3`, 8 of 36 in `2026-09-08-bench-e1-haiku-vs-sonnet-t3`, 7 of 36 in `2026-09-08-bench-e1-sonnet-vs-opus-t3`, 6 of 32 in `2026-09-08-bench-e2-harness-vs-product-t5`, 7 of 18 in `2026-09-08-bench-e3-attempts1-t3`, 3 of 18 in `2026-09-08-bench-e3-baseline-t3`, 15 of 18 in `2026-09-08-bench-e4-knowledge-pack-t3`, and 9 of 16 in `2026-09-08-bench-h1-harness-loop-t5`. The commonest form is a cell that runs `cd <run directory> && cat plan.json run.log` and then diffs its own source against a sibling's.
12	
13	Two went further than reading. In `2026-09-07-bench-h1-harness-loop-t2` the `code:csv-codec` cell `cell-cUuWY2` ran `cp cell-cUuWY2/src/csv.js cell-R8QtdK/src/csv.js`, putting its own solution into the other repetition of its own task, so the second repetition's verdict measures the first cell's work. In `2026-09-08-bench-e2-harness-vs-product-t5` the first `code:sheet-eval` cell `cell-Cr3CtN` wrote its whole solution into the second cell's workspace, `cell-XNKQXT`. Both runs are paired experiments whose statistic is a per-environment difference between two arms; a cell that writes into another cell's workspace breaks the independence the resampling assumes, and a cell that reads the plan knows which arm it is.
14	
15	No cell implemented by the out-of-process product left its workspace in any record. Nothing enforced that either: those cells run a foreign agent in the workspace with its own tool stack, and the harness session that holds their certificate records no tool call at all, so a delegated cell's zero is what this process can see rather than what the delegate did.
16	
17	## Proposal
18	
19	The run seals the cell's workspace against the directory it sits in, for exactly as long as the run lasts.
20	
21	[`EnvironmentRunner.run()`](../../../../packages/improvement/environment-runner/src/index.ts) calls `ctx.readBarrier.denyFor(agent.session, dirname(request.workspace))` after creating the cell agent and disposes the registration when the run ends, so the denial covers the attempts, the check executions, and nothing outside them. A composition without a barrier gets a no-op disposer, which is what its `isolation: none` claim already states.
22	
23	`denyFor` is the per-session sibling of the barrier's existing `protect()`: it adds one directory to the denied set of ONE session, keyed per registration so two registrations of one path both hold. The runner's own session and every other cell's session keep reading the directory; only the cell that owns the workspace is denied it.
24	
25	A denial that covers the parent covers the workspace too, so the policy carries the workspace beside the denied set and the two are ordered. `ReadBarrierPolicy` gains `granted` — the session's cwd — and one rule governs every enforcement dialect: **a denied directory that is a STRICT ancestor of the granted workspace denies the rest of that ancestor's subtree and leaves the workspace whole; a denied directory that IS the workspace, or that lies inside it, denies exactly as it would without the grant.** The rule is expressed four times, once per dialect that can open a path:
26	
27	- the in-process fs gate tests containment in `denies()`, and carves a denial out only for the ancestor the grant lies strictly beneath;
28	- bwrap applies filesystem operations in argv order, so the ancestor's `tmpfs` is mounted, the workspace is bound back from the host, and any denied root inside the workspace is `tmpfs`-mounted after that;
29	- Landlock rulesets are allow-lists with no deny form, so the carve-out of `/` excludes the ancestor's subtree and the workspace is then granted back as its own rule, itself carved around any denial inside it;
30	- Seatbelt evaluates SBPL forms in order with the last match winning, so the ancestor's `deny file-read*` comes first, the workspace's `allow file-read*` after it, and every other denial last.
31	
32	What the barrier refuses is counted where a reader already looks. The run report carries `escapesDenied`, the scorekeeper folds `read-barrier/denied` into `tools.escapesDenied` and sums it per scoreboard row, and [the observatory](../../../../packages/improvement/observatory/README.md) publishes that sum in its own column beside the tamper column — never merged with it, because a refused read is a cell that tried to leave its workspace and a tamper is a cell that changed the files it was measured with.
33	
34	The bench and the live district compose the confinement the [read barrier](2026-09-05-read-barrier.md) already defines: the local sandbox provider, the sandbox policy in `workspace-write` mode, `dsh-bash-sandbox` in place of `dsh-bash-local`, the barrier, and the fs read gate. Both stay at `isolation: none`, because both delegate some cells to the product and the runner refuses an out-of-process implementer under a higher claim. The bench's `route-only` overlay, whose arms all run on the session's own route, patches the runner and the barrier to `isolation: process`, which is the claim its executors can prove.
35	
36	## The denied directory is the parent, not each sibling
37	
38	Denying each sibling cell would stop the copying and leave the leak. The run directory holds `plan.json` and the run log as well as the cells, so listing it or reading one file in it tells the model the experiment it is part of: which arm it is, how many repetitions there are, which environments the plan holds, and what the other cells already did. That is a model-visible input the session log cannot reconstruct and the composition never intended, and it is available from the directory itself without touching a sibling.
39	
40	Denying the parent also holds while the fleet is still writing it. A sibling list computed when the run starts is stale the moment the next cell's workspace is created; the parent is one path known before the agent exists, and every cell the fleet adds later falls under it. The workspace survives because the grant is ordered against the denial, not because the denial enumerated what to skip.
41	
42	## The product arm stays unconfined, and the census audits it
43	
44	An out-of-process implementer brings its own tool stack, its own settings, and its own process tree. `dsh-subagent-claude-code` registers `enforceByRefusal('subagent')` for exactly that reason: under `isolation: process` or `host` the barrier refuses every implementer start, and under `none` the capability runs and denies nothing. A bench whose candidate arm is that provider therefore cannot raise its claim without refusing the arm it exists to measure, so the base composition stays at `none` and the harness-side confinement it does compose binds the cell agents it does own.
45	
46	That leaves the delegated arm audited rather than fenced. The census is the audit: it reads the recorded session logs and reports what each cell's own tool calls named, and it says plainly that a delegated cell records none, so its zero is the absence of evidence. A comparison between the two arms has to carry that asymmetry — the route arm is confined and counted, the delegated arm is neither — rather than read two zeroes as one fact.
47	
48	## What the earlier records lose
49	
50	Every record dated 2026-09-08 or earlier ran unconfined in the sibling layout, so its rows are measurements of cells that could see the experiment. The census gives the per-record counts and [`data/proving-ground/README.md`](../../../../data/proving-ground/README.md) states them before the runs table. What a reader loses depends on the record: a cell that only listed the run directory read the plan and the log, so its transcript contains an input the composition never meant to give it and the log cannot reconstruct; a cell that diffed a sibling's source saw another cell's solution to the same task, so its attempt count is not the number of attempts an isolated cell would need; and the two cells that copied or wrote into another workspace make the affected repetition's verdict a measurement of the other cell. The affected paired experiments — the tier-2 `h1-harness-loop` record and the tier-5 `e2-harness-vs-product` record — are reread as upper bounds on the route arm, not as the difference they state, until they are rerun confined.
51	
52	## Alternatives considered
53	
54	**Give each cell a run directory of its own.** One directory per cell, with the plan and the log somewhere else, removes the sibling layout instead of fencing it. It also removes the fleet's ability to write one plan beside the cells it plans, changes every recorded run's layout, and leaves a cell free to walk to wherever the plan moved. The denial is one registration in the runner; the layout is the fleet's, the recorder's, and every existing record's.
55	
56	**Deny each sibling cell as it is created.** This stops the copying and the diffing, and leaves the plan and the run log readable, which is the larger leak. It also needs a registration per cell per run, kept current while the fleet is still creating workspaces, where the parent is one path known before the first agent exists.
57	
58	**Confine with the workspace root alone, and drop the read barrier.** `dsh-sandbox-policy` in `workspace-write` mode already confines WRITES to the workspace, so the copy into a sibling would have failed. Reads stay open under every mode: `deniedReadRoots` is what expresses a read denial, and it comes from the barrier. Composing the sandbox without the barrier would have stopped one of the two incidents and none of the reading.
59	
60	**Make the workspace grant a sandbox-policy field instead of a barrier one.** The grant exists to order a denial the barrier owns, and the barrier is the one place that knows the session's role. A policy field would let a deployment grant a workspace the barrier never denied an ancestor of, and the two would disagree about what a certificate means. `grantedReadRoot` on the execution policy is the barrier's answer carried to the backends, not a second source of it.
61	
62	**Count refused reads as tool errors.** The scoreboard already counts `toolErrors`, and a refusal often surfaces as one. It is not the same fact: a refusal is recorded whether or not the tool that asked reported an error, and a row that mixed them could not distinguish a cell that tried to leave its workspace from one whose command failed. `escapesDenied` is its own column for the same reason `tampered` is.
63	
64	## Acceptance criteria
65	
66	- Over [`examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/sealed-cell/`](../../../../examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/sealed-cell/cordis.yml), a Loader-booted composition laid out the way a fleet lays one out — a plan, a run log, and two `cell-*` workspaces side by side — runs the registered environment in one of them and certifies it: the cell reads the file staged in its workspace, creates the file its check measures, and the sibling's own file is unchanged. Its confined shell's listing of the parent names neither the sibling, nor the plan, nor the run log, and both files it tried to copy out of the run directory stay empty. [The e2e](../../../../packages/improvement/environment-runner/tests/sealed-cell.e2e.ts) runs on the backend `dsh-sandbox-local` resolves on the host, probed in the provider's own chain order, and skips with a named reason only where none can confine.
67	- The `read` tool's refusal of `../plan.json` in that run appends one `read-barrier/denied` record naming the `fs` capability, the run report carries `escapesDenied: 1`, and a scoreboard row over that session carries the same count.
68	- Unit specs pin the precedence rule at its edges in the fs gate and in each backend dialect: a denied root that is the workspace's parent, one that is a grandparent, one that IS the workspace, and one inside the workspace.
69	- `pnpm run verify-cordis-config` and `pnpm run verify-village-composition` accept the bench, its five overlays, and the live district, and the keyless bench e2e still registers and admits every task.
70	- `census-escapes.mjs` reports every recorded run, and `record-run.mjs` prints the census with each record it writes.
71	
72	## Risks
73	
74	The denial is only as strong as the backend under it. On a host where no sandbox backend can confine a command, `dsh-bash-sandbox` fails closed and the cell's shell cannot run at all, so a bench run on such a host fails rather than measuring an unconfined cell — a louder outcome than the defect, but an outcome.
75	
76	`escapesDenied` counts attempts, not cells. One cell that reads the run directory ten times and ten cells that read it once produce the same row total. That is deliberate — a repeated attempt is a different fact from a single one — but a reader comparing rows has to know it, and the per-cell breakdown lives in the census, not the row.
77	
78	The census's third reason, a `..` opening a path, is a heuristic over shell commands: quoted data inside an embedded script — a URI reference such as `../g` — reads the same as a path. Over this corpus it accounts for three calls, one of them wrong, and no cell count depends on it; the tool counts the reasons apart so a total that rests on it is visible. The two other reasons match literal run-tree paths and are exact.
79	
80	A cell can still read everything outside the run tree that the sandbox mode allows. The barrier denies the experiment, not the host: under `workspace-write` the confined process keeps a read-only view of the rest of the filesystem, so a cell that knows where the repository is could read the environment definitions from it. The fixture material the checks restore is what makes that detectable, and no recorded run has done it.

340	/** One department a killed process left behind, as the next one finds it. */
341	interface SeedDepartment {
342	  readonly key: string
343	  /** Whether the department's own log carries a certificate. */
344	  certified?: boolean
345	  /** Whether the department's worktree still exists; a directory alone when `session` is false. */
346	  worktree?: boolean
347	  /** Whether a department session exists at all. */
348	  session?: boolean
349	  /** Whether that session carries a goal. */
350	  goal?: boolean
351	  /** Whether that session carries an authored standard. */
352	  standard?: boolean
353	  /** Whether the department's goal is blocked. */
354	  blocked?: boolean
355	}
356	
357	/** What one seeded ledger records beyond its own start. */
358	interface SeedOptions {
359	  /** Whether the ledger declares every goal of the spec pending. */
360	  pending?: boolean
361	  /** Whether the ledger records a certified integration over its running one. */
362	  integration?: 'running' | 'certified'
363	  /** A closing record, making the seeded ledger a finished one. */
364	  end?: { outcome: 'released' | 'failed'; mergedRevision?: string }
365	}
366	
367	/** One persisted program a process left open, plus the roots it lives in. */
368	interface SeededProgram {
369	  readonly sessions: string
370	  readonly root: string
371	  readonly programId: string
372	}
373	
374	/**
375	 * Write the durable state a killed process leaves behind: a ledger, one
376	 * department session per key it created, and the worktrees those departments
377	 * own. The seeding harness waits for a Loader that never settles, so its own
378	 * reconciliation never observes the state being written for the next process.
379	 */
380	async function seedProgram(
381	  program: ProgramSpec,
382	  departments: readonly SeedDepartment[] = [],
383	  options: SeedOptions = {},
384	  shared: { sessions?: string; root?: string } = {},
385	): Promise<SeededProgram> {
386	  const sessions = shared.sessions ?? mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'program-sessions-'))
387	  const root = shared.root ?? mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'program-root-'))
388	  if (shared.sessions === undefined) roots.push(sessions)
389	  if (shared.root === undefined) roots.push(root)
390	  const frozen = resolveProgramSpec(program)
391	  const programId = programIdFor(programSpecDigest(frozen))
392	  const seeder = await mount({}, {
393	    sessions,
394	    root,
395	    script: passing,
396	    loader: { await: () => new Promise<void>(() => {}) },
397	  })
398	
399	  const ledger = seeder.ctx.sessions.create(SessionId(programId), { meta: { cwd: root } })
400	  ledger.append('program/start', {
401	    programId,
402	    specSha256: programSpecDigest(frozen),
403	    spec: frozen,
404	    baseRevision: frozen.baseRevision,
405	    implementer: frozen.implementer,
406	  })
407	  if (options.pending !== false) {
408	    for (const entry of frozen.goals) {
409	      ledger.append('program/goal', { programId, key: entry.key, status: 'pending' })
410	    }
411	  }
412	  for (const department of departments) {
413	    const sessionId = `${programId}-${department.key}` as SessionId
414	    const workspace = join(root, programId, department.key)
415	    if (department.worktree !== false) mkdirSync(workspace, { recursive: true })
416	    if (department.session === false) continue
417	    ledger.append('program/goal', { programId, key: department.key, status: 'running', sessionId, workspace })
418	    const goalSpec = frozen.goals.find(entry => entry.key === department.key) as ProgramGoalSpec
419	    const session = seeder.ctx.sessions.create(sessionId, { meta: { cwd: workspace } })
420	    const agent = stubAgent(session)
421	    const unregister = seeder.ctx.agents.register(agent)
422	    session.append('program/member', { programId, key: department.key })
423	    if (department.goal !== false) {
424	      const created = seeder.ctx.goals.create(agent, { objective: goalSpec.objective, maxGoalRounds: 2 })
425	      seeder.ctx.goals.disarm(agent)
426	      if (department.blocked === true) {
427	        seeder.ctx.goals.block(agent, { id: created.id, revision: created.revision }, {
428	          code: 'budget-exhausted',
429	          message: 'the department spent its caps',
430	        })
431	      } else if (department.standard !== false) {
432	        const standard = seeder.ctx.completionStandards.author(agent, { goalId: created.id, checks: goalSpec.checks })
433	        if (department.certified === true) {
434	          seeder.ctx.completionStandards.recordRun(agent, { id: standard.id, revision: standard.revision }, 'none',
435	            goalSpec.checks.map(check => ({ checkId: check.id, status: 'pass' as const, evidence: 'exit 0' })),
436	            { executor: 'runner' })
437	          seeder.ctx.goals.complete(agent, { id: created.id, revision: created.revision })
438	        }
439	      }
440	    }
441	    await seeder.ctx.sessions.flush(session)
442	    unregister()
443	  }
444	  if (options.integration !== undefined) {
445	    ledger.append('program/integration', { programId, status: 'running' })
446	    if (options.integration === 'certified') {
447	      ledger.append('program/integration', { programId, status: 'certified' })
448	    }
449	  }
450	  if (options.end !== undefined) ledger.append('program/end', { programId, ...options.end })
451	  await seeder.ctx.sessions.flush(ledger)
452	  await seeder.dispose()
453	  harnesses.splice(harnesses.indexOf(seeder), 1)
454	  return { sessions, root, programId }
455	}

1	/**
2	 * Keyless REAL-composition coverage for the program ledger: three boots of one
3	 * `cordis.yml` over one persistence root and one temporary git repository. The
4	 * first runs a two-goal program with a dependency to its release; the second
5	 * starts a different program and dies the moment its first department is
6	 * recorded certified; the third reconciles that program from the department's
7	 * own log, starts only the goal that never ran, and releases.
8	 *
9	 * The mock implementer commits nothing, so each department branch head is the
10	 * base revision and the integration merges are already up to date. What the
11	 * fixture proves is the ledger, the department sessions and worktrees, the
12	 * per-session caps, and the reconciliation — not what a model can build.
13	 */
14	
15	import { mkdtemp, rm } from 'node:fs/promises'
16	import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
17	import { join } from 'node:path'
18	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
19	import { afterAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
20	import { LOADER_SMOKE_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS, runLoaderSmoke } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-loader-smoke'
21	import type { ProgramEnd, ProgramGoalRecord, ProgramIntegrationRecord, ProgramResume, ProgramStart } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-program'
22	
23	const binScript = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../../examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/program/driver.ts', import.meta.url))
24	const configPath = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../../examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/program/cordis.yml', import.meta.url))
25	const repoTsconfig = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../../tsconfig.json', import.meta.url))
26	
27	/** Three boots, each a full mock-model program, need more than the default window. */
28	const PHASE_TIMEOUT_MS = 180_000
29	const KILLED = 9
30	const RESTART_LABEL = 'restart'
31	
32	interface LedgerLine {
33	  sessionId: string
34	  events: { type: string; data: unknown }[]
35	  signoffs: string[]
36	}
37	
38	interface MemberLine {
39	  sessionId: string
40	  programId: string
41	  key: string
42	  certified: boolean
43	  caps: unknown
44	}
45	
46	interface DriverResult {
47	  type: string
48	  report: { programId: string; sessionId: string; outcome?: string; mergedRevision?: string; goals: { key: string; status: string }[] }
49	  ledgers: LedgerLine[]
50	  members: MemberLine[]
51	}
52	
53	const roots: string[] = []
54	
55	afterAll(async () => {
56	  await Promise.all(roots.splice(0).map(root => rm(root, { recursive: true, force: true })))
57	})

59	/** Boot the driver once over the shared persistence root and repository. */
60	async function phase(
61	  sessions: string,
62	  repository: string,
63	  env: Record<string, string>,
64	  expectedExitCode = 0,
65	): Promise<string> {
66	  const { stdout, stderr } = await runLoaderSmoke({
67	    label: `program (${JSON.stringify(env)})`,
68	    tempDirPrefix: 'program-e2e-',
69	    binScript,
70	    libBinScript: binScript,
71	    configPath,
72	    binArgs: [configPath],
73	    tsconfigPath: repoTsconfig,
74	    processTimeoutMs: PHASE_TIMEOUT_MS,
75	    expectedExitCode,
76	    env: { DSH_TEST_SESSION_ROOT: sessions, DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_REPO: repository, ...env },
77	  })
78	  expect(stderr).toBe('')
79	  return stdout
80	}
81	
82	/** The last JSON line the driver printed. */
83	function result(stdout: string): DriverResult {
84	  const parsed = JSON.parse(stdout.trimEnd().split('\n').at(-1) ?? '') as DriverResult
85	  expect(parsed.type).toBe('result')
86	  return parsed
87	}
88	
89	/** The ledger of one program, by the session id its own start event carries. */
90	function ledgerOf(observed: DriverResult, programId: string): LedgerLine {
91	  const found = observed.ledgers.find(ledger => ledger.sessionId === programId)
92	  expect(found, `no ledger for ${programId}`).toBeDefined()
93	  return found as LedgerLine
94	}
95	
96	/** The statuses one ledger recorded for one goal key, in log order. */
97	function statuses(ledger: LedgerLine, key: string): string[] {
98	  return ledger.events
99	    .filter(event => event.type === 'program/goal' && (event.data as ProgramGoalRecord).key === key)
100	    .map(event => (event.data as ProgramGoalRecord).status)
101	}
102	
103	describe('the program ledger through a real cordis.yml, killed and restarted', () => {
104	  it('releases a two-goal program, then reconciles a killed one and releases it too', async () => {
105	    const sessions = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'program-sessions-'))
106	    const repository = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'program-repo-'))
107	    roots.push(sessions, repository)
108	
109	    const first = result(await phase(sessions, repository, {}))
110	    expect(first.report.outcome).toBe('released')
111	    expect(first.report.goals.map(goal => [goal.key, goal.status])).toEqual([['api', 'merged'], ['docs', 'merged']])
112	
113	    const ledger = ledgerOf(first, first.report.programId)
114	    const opened = ledger.events[0]?.data as ProgramStart
115	    expect(ledger.events[0]?.type).toBe('program/start')
116	    expect(opened.programId).toBe(first.report.programId)
117	    expect(opened.specSha256).toBe(first.report.programId.replace('program-', ''))
118	    expect(opened.baseRevision).toBe('base')
119	    expect(opened.signoff).toEqual({ artefactSha256: 'f'.repeat(64) })
120	    // Both signatures the deployment requires live in the program's own log.
121	    expect(ledger.signoffs).toEqual(['spec-freeze', 'release'])
122	
123	    // The dependent goal only ever runs after the goal it depends on certified.
124	    expect(statuses(ledger, 'api')).toEqual(['pending', 'running', 'certified', 'merged'])
125	    expect(statuses(ledger, 'docs')).toEqual(['pending', 'running', 'certified', 'merged'])
126	    const integrations = ledger.events.filter(event => event.type === 'program/integration')
127	      .map(event => (event.data as ProgramIntegrationRecord).status)
128	    expect(integrations).toEqual(['running', 'certified'])
129	    const closing = ledger.events.at(-1)?.data as ProgramEnd
130	    expect(ledger.events.at(-1)?.type).toBe('program/end')
131	    expect(closing.outcome).toBe('released')
132	    expect(closing.mergedRevision).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{40}$/)
133	
134	    // Every department and the integration is a member session of its program,
135	    // each carrying its own certificate and, for a department, its own caps.
136	    const members = first.members.filter(member => member.programId === first.report.programId)
137	    expect(members.map(member => member.key).sort()).toEqual(['@integration', 'api', 'docs'])
138	    expect(members.every(member => member.certified)).toBe(true)
139	    expect(members.filter(member => member.key !== '@integration').map(member => member.caps)).toEqual([
140	      { maxTotalTokens: 400_000, maxWallMs: 300_000 },
141	      { maxTotalTokens: 400_000, maxWallMs: 300_000 },
142	    ])
143	
144	    // A second program over the same repository dies as its first department is
145	    // recorded certified, leaving a ledger with no closing record.
146	    await phase(sessions, repository, {
147	      DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_LABEL: RESTART_LABEL,
148	      DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_KILL_AFTER_CERTIFIED: '1',
149	    }, KILLED)
150	
151	    const third = result(await phase(sessions, repository, { DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_LABEL: RESTART_LABEL }))
152	    expect(third.report.programId).not.toBe(first.report.programId)
153	    expect(third.report.outcome).toBe('released')
154	
155	    const restarted = ledgerOf(third, third.report.programId)
156	    const resumed = restarted.events.filter(event => event.type === 'program/resume')
157	      .map(event => (event.data as ProgramResume).statuses)
158	    expect(resumed).toHaveLength(1)
159	    // The killed process left one certified department and one that never started.
160	    expect(resumed[0]).toMatchObject({ pending: 1, certified: 1, running: 0 })
161	    // `api` is recorded certified once, by whichever process observed it first;
162	    // it is never started again, and `docs` starts only in the third boot.
163	    expect(statuses(restarted, 'api').filter(status => status === 'running')).toHaveLength(1)
164	    expect(statuses(restarted, 'api').at(-1)).toBe('merged')
165	    expect(statuses(restarted, 'docs')).toEqual(['pending', 'running', 'certified', 'merged'])
166	
167	    // One session per key, for every key of the restarted program.
168	    const restartedMembers = third.members.filter(member => member.programId === third.report.programId)
169	    expect(restartedMembers.map(member => member.key).sort()).toEqual(['@integration', 'api', 'docs'])
170	    expect(new Set(restartedMembers.map(member => member.sessionId)).size).toBe(3)
171	  }, PHASE_TIMEOUT_MS * 3 + LOADER_SMOKE_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS)
172	})

1	#!/usr/bin/env node
2	/**
3	 * Test driver: create the temporary git repository the program delivers into,
4	 * boot the program composition, run one two-goal program with a dependency to
5	 * its release, and print every program ledger plus the member stamps the
6	 * department and integration sessions left in the persistence root.
7	 *
8	 * With `DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_KILL_AFTER_CERTIFIED` set, the driver instead exits
9	 * hard the moment the ledger records the first department as certified — the
10	 * department's own certificate is durable by then, while the program session
11	 * may or may not have recorded it, which is exactly the state the next boot
12	 * reconciles.
13	 */
14	
15	import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process'
16	import { existsSync, mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
17	import { join } from 'node:path'
18	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
19	import { boot, resolveConfigPath } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot'
20	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader'
21	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
22	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-default-model'
23	import { programIdFor, programSpecDigest, resolveProgramSpec } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-program'
24	import type { ProgramSpec } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-program'
25	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-program'
26	import { SessionId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
27	import type { SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
28	import type { SessionPersistence } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence'
29	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-signoff'
30	import type { CheckId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification/types'
31	
32	/** Exit code the kill switch leaves behind, distinct from every clean exit. */
33	const KILLED = 9
34	
35	/** The artefact both of the program's signatures attest. */
36	const ARTEFACT = 'f'.repeat(64)
37	
38	/** One program session's ledger as the e2e asserts on it. */
39	interface LedgerLine {
40	  readonly sessionId: string
41	  readonly events: { readonly type: string; readonly data: unknown }[]
42	  /** Transitions the same session was signed for, in log order. */
43	  readonly signoffs: string[]
44	}
45	
46	/** One member session's stamp as the e2e asserts on it. */
47	interface MemberLine {
48	  readonly sessionId: string
49	  readonly programId: string
50	  readonly key: string
51	  /** Whether the member's own log carries a certificate. */
52	  readonly certified: boolean
53	  /** The caps the member session recorded for itself. */
54	  readonly caps: unknown
55	}
56	
57	const configPath = process.argv[2]
58	if (configPath === undefined) throw new Error('program driver requires a config path')
59	
60	const repository = process.env.DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_REPO
61	if (repository === undefined) throw new Error('program driver requires DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_REPO')
62	
63	// The roster's root has to be absolute and the smoke runs in an isolated
64	// temporary cwd, so the presets beside this file are exported by path.
65	process.env.DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_PRESETS = fileURLToPath(new URL('presets', import.meta.url))
66	
67	// A host that configures git through `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` hands every child a
68	// command-line config the shell seam cannot forward whole: `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_*`
69	// is credential-shaped, so the scrub drops the keys and keeps the count, and
70	// git then refuses every invocation. The fixture runs against its own
71	// repository, so it drops the whole set rather than inheriting half of it.
72	for (const name of Object.keys(process.env)) {
73	  if (name.startsWith('GIT_CONFIG_')) Reflect.deleteProperty(process.env, name)
74	}
75	
76	/** Create the repository the program delivers into, once, with a tagged base commit. */
77	function ensureRepository(root: string): void {
78	  if (existsSync(join(root, '.git'))) return
79	  mkdirSync(root, { recursive: true })
80	  const git = (...args: string[]): void => void execFileSync('git', args, { cwd: root, stdio: 'pipe' })
81	  git('init', '-q', '.')
82	  git('config', 'user.email', 'program@example.test')
83	  git('config', 'user.name', 'program fixture')
84	  writeFileSync(join(root, 'base.txt'), 'base\n')
85	  git('add', 'base.txt')
86	  git('commit', '-qm', 'base')
87	  git('tag', 'base')
88	}
89	
90	/** The program the fixture runs: two goals, the second delivered after the first. */
91	function programSpec(label: string): ProgramSpec {
92	  const budget = { maxTotalTokens: 400_000, maxWallMs: 300_000 }
93	  return {
94	    objective: `deliver the ${label} release`,
95	    baseRevision: 'base',
96	    signoff: { artefactSha256: ARTEFACT },
97	    goals: [
98	      {
99	        key: 'api',
100	        objective: 'Deliver the api of this program on its own branch.',
101	        preset: 'implementing',
102	        isolation: 'none',
103	        budget,
104	        dependsOn: [],
105	        checks: [{ id: 'api-base-present' as CheckId, outcome: 'the branch still carries the base file', run: 'test -f base.txt' }],
106	      },
107	      {
108	        key: 'docs',
109	        objective: 'Document the api of this program on its own branch.',
110	        preset: 'documenting',
111	        isolation: 'none',
112	        budget,
113	        dependsOn: ['api'],
114	        checks: [{ id: 'docs-base-present' as CheckId, outcome: 'the branch still carries the base file', run: 'test -f base.txt' }],
115	      },
116	    ],
117	    integration: {
118	      checks: [{ id: 'merged-base-present' as CheckId, outcome: 'the merged head carries the base file', run: 'test -f base.txt' }],
119	      gates: ['test -r base.txt'],
120	    },
121	  }
122	}
123	
124	/** Every program ledger and every member stamp in the persistence root. */
125	async function readRoot(persistence: SessionPersistence): Promise<{ ledgers: LedgerLine[]; members: MemberLine[] }> {
126	  const ledgers: LedgerLine[] = []
127	  const members: MemberLine[] = []
128	  for (const stored of await persistence.list()) {
129	    const { events } = await persistence.inspect(stored.id)
130	    const programEvents = events.filter((event: SessionEvent) => event.type.startsWith('program/') && event.type !== 'program/member')
131	    if (programEvents.length > 0) {
132	      ledgers.push({
133	        sessionId: stored.id,
134	        events: programEvents.map(event => ({ type: event.type, data: event.data })),
135	        signoffs: events.flatMap(event => (event.type === 'signoff/recorded' ? [event.data.transition] : [])),
136	      })
137	    }
138	    for (const event of events) {
139	      if (event.type !== 'program/member') continue
140	      members.push({
141	        sessionId: stored.id,
142	        programId: event.data.programId,
143	        key: event.data.key,
144	        certified: events.some(candidate => candidate.type === 'verification/certificate'),
145	        caps: events.find(candidate => candidate.type === 'budget/caps')?.data,
146	      })
147	    }
148	  }
149	  return { ledgers, members }
150	}
151	
152	/**
153	 * Record the spec-freeze and release signatures on the program session, the way
154	 * a client district's signer would before the program starts. A session that
155	 * already carries them is left alone, so a resumed phase signs nothing twice.
156	 */
157	async function sign(ctx: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof boot>>, spec: ProgramSpec, cwd: string): Promise<void> {
158	  const sessionId = SessionId(programIdFor(programSpecDigest(resolveProgramSpec(spec))))
159	  const signoffs = ctx.get('signoffs')
160	  const agents = ctx.get('agents')
161	  if (signoffs === undefined || agents === undefined) throw new Error('program driver requires the signoffs and agents services')
162	  if ((await ctx.get('sessionPersistence')?.list() ?? []).some(stored => stored.id === sessionId)) return
163	  const model = ctx.get('agentDefaultModel')?.currentSelection()
164	  if (model === undefined) throw new Error('program driver requires the default-model service')
165	  const handle = await agents.create({
166	    sessionId,
167	    meta: { cwd },
168	    agentOptions: { provider: model.provider, model: model.model },
169	  })
170	  try {
171	    for (const transition of ['spec-freeze', 'release'] as const) {
172	      signoffs.record(handle.agent, {
173	        transition,
174	        principal: { kind: 'human', id: 'program-fixture', displayName: 'Program Fixture' },
175	        artefactSha256: ARTEFACT,
176	        evidence: [{ kind: 'spec', ref: 'the frozen program spec' }],
177	      })
178	    }
179	    await ctx.sessions.flush(handle.agent.session)
180	  } finally {
181	    await handle.dispose()
182	  }
183	}
184	
185	// The repository has to exist before the program plugin validates its
186	// workspaceRoot, so it is minted before the composition loads.
187	ensureRepository(repository)
188	
189	const ctx = await boot('program-e2e', resolveConfigPath(configPath, undefined))
190	try {
191	  // Loader siblings mount concurrently; the program mounts presets and reads
192	  // persisted sessions, so the driver drives only the settled application.
193	  await ctx.get('loader')?.await()
194	  const programs = ctx.get('programs')
195	  const persistence = ctx.get('sessionPersistence')
196	  if (programs === undefined || persistence === undefined) throw new Error('program driver requires the programs and session persistence services')
197	  if (process.env.DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_KILL_AFTER_CERTIFIED === '1') {
198	    ctx.on('session/event', (_session, event) => {
199	      if (event.type === 'program/goal' && event.data.status === 'certified') process.exit(KILLED)
200	    })
201	  }
202	  const spec = programSpec(process.env.DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_LABEL ?? 'first')
203	  // The program id is the spec digest, so the two signatures the deployment
204	  // requires are recorded on that session before the program opens it. A second
205	  // phase resuming the same root finds them already there.
206	  await sign(ctx, spec, repository)
207	  const report = await programs.start(spec)
208	  const observed = await readRoot(persistence)
209	  process.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify({ type: 'result', report, ...observed })}\n`)
210	} finally {
211	  await ctx.fiber.dispose()
212	}

# AGENTS.md — Examples

Runnable harness compositions. `examples/` is one workspace member and the module-resolution root for runnable and test Cordis configs; it is not a build target. [package.json](package.json) declares the packages loaded by those configs, while each leaf's private `package.json` remains metadata only.

Extract reusable logic into `packages/`, where per-file coverage and README gates apply. Examples keep only `cordis.yml` wiring, demo artifacts, and e2e/snapshot scenarios; app package bins own boot glue.

## E2E smokes

Each example has both:

- **Keyless:** boot the real `cordis.yml` through the Loader, drive it, and assert output and clean exit. Catches invalid Loader exports that hand-mounted tests miss ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **With-key:** send a live-model prompt and verify external state, not the model's claim. Self-skip without `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`; see [testing.md](../docs/testing.md).

Keyless process smokes use `@deepseek-ai/dsh-loader-smoke` for Loader launch resolution; terminal tests wrap that launch in a pseudo-terminal. Tests supply paths, environment, input, and assertions. Every checked-in test Cordis config lives under its corresponding `examples/<agent>/` leaf. Map a package-owned config to `examples/<agent>/tests/fixtures/<group>/<package>/cordis.yml`, keep its driver and assertions package-local, and declare every package it names in both root `tsconfig.json` references and `examples/package.json`.

Do not inventory example tests here; the `tests/` trees and root scripts are authoritative.

In `cordis.yml`, comment only non-obvious wiring, load-order consequences, replay, security boundaries, and configuration scope. Do not narrate visible entries; use [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for required coverage and editorial judgment.

See [the root AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) for repo-wide conventions and [docs/architecture.md](../docs/architecture.md) for the design.

2	 * Package-owned invariant: the program ledger is what a restarted process reads
3	 * to decide which department to start, so its five relations hold in every
4	 * session a program writes to. Every `program/goal`, `program/integration`,
5	 * `program/resume`, and `program/end` follows a `program/start` of the same
6	 * program in the same session — a record naming another program would attribute
7	 * a department, a merge, or a release to a session that never ran it. A goal's
8	 * status moves only along the transitions the ledger admits, so a reconciliation
9	 * cannot silently rewrite a department's history. `merged` follows a certified
10	 * integration, because the merge commit that makes a branch merged is the
11	 * integration's own; and `program/end { released }` follows the same certified
12	 * integration, because the certificate over the merged head is what a release
13	 * claims. In a department session, every `program/delegation` follows that
14	 * session's `program/member` for the same key and advances the attempt, which
15	 * is what makes "a delegated attempt that ended is never run again" a property
16	 * of the log rather than of a reconciliation.
17	 *
18	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-program/invariant
19	 */

21	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
22	import { sessionEventValidator } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-invariants'
23	import type { InvariantFailure, InvariantInstaller } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-invariants'
24	import type { SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
25	import type { ProgramGoalStatus, ProgramIntegrationStatus } from './types.ts'
26	
27	const PACKAGE_NAME = '@deepseek-ai/dsh-program'
28	
29	/** Cordis companion plugin name. */
30	export const name = 'program-invariant'
31	/** Service required before the companion can reserve package ownership. */
32	export const inject = ['invariants']
33	
34	/**
35	 * Statuses one goal may move to from each status it holds. A key with no record
36	 * yet enters at `pending`, so a ledger states every goal of the spec before it
37	 * states what became of any of them.
38	 */
39	const GOAL_TRANSITIONS: Readonly<Record<ProgramGoalStatus, readonly ProgramGoalStatus[]>> = {
40	  pending: ['running', 'failed', 'abandoned'],
41	  running: ['blocked', 'certified', 'failed'],
42	  blocked: ['running', 'failed', 'abandoned'],
43	  certified: ['merged', 'failed'],
44	  merged: [],
45	  failed: [],
46	  abandoned: [],
47	}
48	
49	/**
50	 * Statuses one integration may move to from each status it holds. It enters at
51	 * `running` once its merged worktree exists, or straight at `failed` when the
52	 * worktree could not be created at all.
53	 */
54	const INTEGRATION_TRANSITIONS: Readonly<Record<ProgramIntegrationStatus, readonly ProgramIntegrationStatus[]>> = {
55	  running: ['certified', 'failed'],
56	  certified: [],
57	  failed: ['running'],
58	}
59	
60	/** The statuses one integration may be recorded at before any record exists. */
61	const INTEGRATION_ENTRY: readonly ProgramIntegrationStatus[] = ['running', 'failed']
62	
63	/** The latest status the prefix recorded for one goal key, absent when it records none. */
64	function latestGoalStatus(prior: readonly SessionEvent[], key: string): ProgramGoalStatus | undefined {
65	  let status: ProgramGoalStatus | undefined
66	  for (const event of prior) {
67	    if (event.type === 'program/goal' && event.data.key === key) status = event.data.status
68	  }
69	  return status
70	}
71	
72	/** The latest integration status the prefix recorded, absent when it records none. */
73	function latestIntegrationStatus(prior: readonly SessionEvent[]): ProgramIntegrationStatus | undefined {
74	  let status: ProgramIntegrationStatus | undefined
75	  for (const event of prior) {
76	    if (event.type === 'program/integration') status = event.data.status
77	  }
78	  return status
79	}
80	
81	/** Whether the prefix carries a certified integration of this program. */
82	function integrationCertified(prior: readonly SessionEvent[]): boolean {
83	  return prior.some(event => event.type === 'program/integration' && event.data.status === 'certified')
84	}
85	
86	/** Report a goal record whose status does not follow the one the prefix recorded. */
87	function checkGoalTransition(prior: readonly SessionEvent[], event: SessionEvent<'program/goal'>, fail: InvariantFailure): void {
88	  const { key, status } = event.data
89	  const previous = latestGoalStatus(prior, key)
90	  if (previous === undefined) {
91	    if (status !== 'pending') {
92	      fail(`session event ${event.seq} records goal "${key}" as ${status}, which this program never declared pending`)
93	    }
94	    return
95	  }
96	  const allowed = GOAL_TRANSITIONS[previous]
97	  if (!allowed.includes(status)) {
98	    fail(`session event ${event.seq} moves goal "${key}" from ${previous} to ${status}, which the ledger does not admit`)
99	  }
100	  if (status === 'merged' && !integrationCertified(prior)) {
101	    fail(`session event ${event.seq} records goal "${key}" as merged before a certified integration`)
102	  }
103	}
104	
105	/**
106	 * Report a delegated attempt this department session cannot own: one for a key
107	 * it is not the department for, or one that does not advance past the attempts
108	 * it already recorded.
109	 */
110	function checkDelegation(prior: readonly SessionEvent[], event: SessionEvent<'program/delegation'>, fail: InvariantFailure): void {
111	  const { goalKey, attempt } = event.data
112	  const stamped = prior.some(candidate => candidate.type === 'program/member' && candidate.data.key === goalKey)
113	  if (!stamped) {
114	    fail(`session event ${event.seq} delegates goal "${goalKey}", which this session is not the department for`)
115	    return
116	  }
117	  for (const candidate of prior) {
118	    if (candidate.type === 'program/delegation' && candidate.data.attempt >= attempt) {
119	      fail(`session event ${event.seq} records delegation attempt ${attempt} of goal "${goalKey}" after attempt ${candidate.data.attempt}, which this session already ran`)
120	      return
121	    }
122	  }
123	}
124	
125	/**
126	 * Report a program event that breaks one of the five relations, reading the
127	 * events that precede it in the same session.
128	 * @param prior - the session's committed events, oldest first.
129	 * @param event - the candidate session event.
130	 * @param fail - the reporter for a broken relation.
131	 */
132	export function checkLedgerEvent(prior: readonly SessionEvent[], event: SessionEvent, fail: InvariantFailure): void {
133	  if (event.type === 'program/delegation') {
134	    checkDelegation(prior, event, fail)
135	    return
136	  }
137	  if (event.type !== 'program/goal' && event.type !== 'program/integration'
138	    && event.type !== 'program/resume' && event.type !== 'program/end') return
139	  const opened = prior.some(candidate => candidate.type === 'program/start'
140	    && candidate.data.programId === event.data.programId)
141	  if (!opened) {
142	    fail(`session event ${event.seq} records ${event.type} for program "${event.data.programId}", which this session never started`)
143	    return
144	  }
145	  if (event.type === 'program/goal') {
146	    checkGoalTransition(prior, event, fail)
147	    return
148	  }
149	  if (event.type === 'program/integration') {
150	    const previous = latestIntegrationStatus(prior)
151	    const allowed = previous === undefined ? INTEGRATION_ENTRY : INTEGRATION_TRANSITIONS[previous]
152	    if (!allowed.includes(event.data.status)) {
153	      fail(`session event ${event.seq} moves the integration from ${previous ?? 'unrecorded'} to ${event.data.status}, which the ledger does not admit`)
154	    }
155	    return
156	  }
157	  if (event.type === 'program/end' && event.data.outcome === 'released' && !integrationCertified(prior)) {
158	    fail(`session event ${event.seq} releases program "${event.data.programId}" without a certified integration`)
159	  }
160	}
161	
162	/** Check existing sessions and every candidate event before Session publishes it. */
163	const install: InvariantInstaller = sessionEventValidator(checkLedgerEvent, ctx => ctx.sessions.list())

/**
 * Run local and CI quality gates with bounded in-process scheduling.
 *
 * Package scripts own public aggregate names; this runner owns their validated
 * dependency graphs, scheduler environment, and process diagnostics.
 * @see ../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-06-parallel-pre-push-gates.md
 */
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { availableParallelism } from 'node:os'
import { resolve } from 'node:path'
import { performance } from 'node:perf_hooks'
import { COVERAGE_EXEMPT_ENV, coverageExemptHeavySuites } from './coverage-exempt.ts'

/** A named aggregate exposed by the gate runner. */
export type Mode =
  | 'ci-primary'
  | 'ci-linux-primary'
  | 'ci-static'
  | 'ci-lint-contracts-ready'
  | 'ci-coverage'
  | 'ci-snapshot'
  | 'ci-artifacts'
  | 'ci-consumers'
  | 'ci-windows-blocking'
  | 'ci-windows-complete'
  | 'ci-windows-observational'
  | 'node-compat'
  | 'check-all'
  | 'doc-sync'

type GateResultStatus = 'passed' | 'failed' | 'skipped'
type GateState = 'pending' | 'running' | GateResultStatus

/** A command and its dependency metadata inside one aggregate. */
export interface Gate {
  id: string
  label: string
  displayCommand: string
  command: string
  args: string[]
  needs?: string[]
  env?: Record<string, string | undefined>
  allowFailure?: boolean
}

/** The observed outcome of one gate process. */
export interface GateResult {
  gate: Gate
  status: GateResultStatus
  durationMs: number
  output: GateOutputChunk[]
  exitCode: number | null
  signalCode: NodeJS.Signals | null
  error?: string
}

interface GateOutputChunk {
  stream: 'stdout' | 'stderr'
  text: string
}

interface RunningGate {
  gate: Gate
  promise: Promise<GateResult>
}

interface ConcurrencyDefault {
  workers: number
  source: string
}

type GateExecutor = (gate: Gate) => Promise<GateResult>
type ResultObserver = (result: GateResult) => void

const root = resolve(import.meta.dirname, '..')
if (import.meta.main) {
  process.exitCode = await main(process.argv.slice(2))
}

async function main(args: string[]): Promise<number> {
  const mode = parseMode(args[0])
  const gates = gatesForMode(mode)
  const concurrencyDefault = defaultConcurrency(mode, gates.length)
  const concurrencyOverride = process.env.DSH_GATE_CONCURRENCY
  const maxConcurrency = concurrencyFromEnv('DSH_GATE_CONCURRENCY', concurrencyDefault.workers)
  const concurrencySource = concurrencyOverride === undefined || concurrencyOverride === ''
    ? concurrencyDefault.source
    : '$DSH_GATE_CONCURRENCY'
  const startedAt = performance.now()
  console.log(`run-gates: ${mode} running ${gates.length} gate(s) with ${maxConcurrency} worker(s) from ${concurrencySource}.`)

  const results = await runGates(gates, maxConcurrency, runGate, printResult)
  printSummary(results, performance.now() - startedAt)
  return results.some(result => result.gate.allowFailure !== true && (result.status === 'failed' || result.status === 'skipped'))
    ? 1
    : 0
}

function parseMode(raw: string | undefined): Mode {
  switch (raw) {
    case 'ci-primary':
    case 'ci-linux-primary':
    case 'ci-static':
    case 'ci-lint-contracts-ready':
    case 'ci-coverage':
    case 'ci-snapshot':
    case 'ci-artifacts':
    case 'ci-consumers':
    case 'ci-windows-blocking':
    case 'ci-windows-complete':
    case 'ci-windows-observational':
    case 'node-compat':
    case 'check-all':
    case 'doc-sync':
      return raw
    default:
      throw new Error(
        `run-gates: expected mode ci-primary | ci-linux-primary | ci-static | ci-lint-contracts-ready | ci-coverage | ci-snapshot | ci-artifacts | ci-consumers | ci-windows-blocking | ci-windows-complete | ci-windows-observational | node-compat | check-all | doc-sync, got ${JSON.stringify(raw)}.`,
      )
  }
